Much like an insurance policy, a lasting power of attorney may lie forgotten inside a drawer, yet its worth is enormous if the situation demands it. Although starting the conversation can feel uncomfortable, making these arrangements early remains a crucial step.

"Everyone should have one," says Leanne Crellin, partner of the Hull-based law firm Bridge McFarland LLP.

"And the sooner the better, because if you lose mental capacity due to old age, illness or injury, you may be deemed unable to manage your affairs."

Money Saving Expert founder Martin Lewis has even urged everyone to pay for a lasting power of attorney that he believes is “more important than a will”.

Speaking on his BBC podcast, he said: "Wills are really important, but in my view, a power of attorney is even more so, which is why it's worrying that far fewer people have them. Best is to have both. But when you're dead, you're dead; it's just a question of where your assets go."

Here is everything you need to understand about establishing this crucial legal safeguard.

What is a power of attorney?

A Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) is split into two legal documents – the Health and Welfare LPA and a Property and Financial Affairs LPA.

She explains, “The financial one is a document that allows you to appoint a person or people to assist you with your financial decisions. The emphasis there is on ‘assist’. The job isn’t to take over, it’s to help you when you can’t make those decisions yourself.”

open image in gallery A Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) is split into two legal documents – the Health and Welfare LPA and a Property and Financial Affairs LPA

When does it come into force and what does it cover?

“It can come into force as soon as it is registered with the Office of Public Guardian (OPG) which provides flexibility if you need help due to physical ailments and frailty in addition to loss of mental capacity,” explains Crellin.

“It covers all of your finances such as access to bank accounts and pensions, payment of bills and dealing with investments. It also covers your property and allows your attorneys to sell your property and buy another if appropriate. This is particularly helpful if you enter a care home.”

How can I set one up?

You can set up a power of attorney through a solicitor or by yourself. Solicitors also act as your certificate provider ensuring that you have the necessary capacity to take out the power of attorney, and they act as a safeguard.

“It’s my job to make sure that the attorneys are appropriate,” she says. “We go through the family tree and if they’re sitting in front of me with a friend or a neighbour, but tell me they’ve got two children, I will ask why aren’t they involved?”

open image in gallery Solicitors also act as your certificate provider ensuring that you have the necessary capacity to take out the power of attorney, and they act as a safeguard

Spotting attorneys are not exerting undue influence is also part of the job.

“You’d be amazed how many times that happens. People see a vulnerable person and just see pound signs,” says Crellin.

“You get better at spotting the red flags. For example, if someone is talking over them and is not allowing them to speak.”

When should you set one up?

In order to make a power of attorney, you must be over 18 and have the mental capacity to do so.

“Mental capacity is the ability to make a specific decision at the time that it needs to be made,” explains Crellin. “And if you do not have a power of attorney in place, no one can help you or access your finances.

“This will leave you in limbo until a court intervention, which can take up to 12 months and can cost thousands. Why leave it to chance?”

open image in gallery Power of attorney exists to give families control over what happens to someone if they suffer an accident or an illness and are unable to make their own decisions ( PA Wire )

She adds that many clients are usually children bringing the parents in because they’ve got to that age where they’re getting a bit forgetful.

“If you see someone struggling, don’t wait until they’ve been diagnosed with dementia, you need to do it straight away because these things can progress quickly,” advises Crellin.

And she accepts that the conversation can be awkward. “People don’t want their parents or loved ones to think they’re after the money, but that document also allows them to apply for benefits that they may need.”

What happens if you don’t have one?

“People think their spouse or next of kin can help, but your finances cannot be accessed and your house cannot be sold,” she says. “This is particularly problematic if you are going into a care home. Social services can issue a DOLs (Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards) for health and welfare but not for finances.”

The only option left is time-consuming and expensive. Crellin says, “Your loved ones will have to apply to the Court of Protection to be appointed as your deputy, and they have to deem this person suitable.”

Can more than one person be named?

“You can appoint more than one main attorney, and you can also appoint one or more replacement attorneys,” says Crellin. “For example, someone may appoint their spouse as their main attorney and their children as replacements.”

She adds, “If appointing more than one attorney, you should appoint them jointly and severally. This allows them to act together but also separately if one of them dies or is unable to act.”

How much does it cost?

“When you register, the OPG charges £92 per application – and you will need two,” says Crellin. “Then there’s the professional fees. We charge £650 (inc VAT) for one or £1,000 (inc VAT) for both.”

Can people set up a power attorney on their own?

“People can find their own certificate provider – that’s the person who’s going to sign the form to say they’ve got capacity,” Crellin explains. “Normally that would be me but they would need someone who’s not a family member and who has known them for some time.”

She warns, “The OPG is very strict and any slight error in signing the forms can result in the power of attorney being rejected.”

Pope Leo XIV, history's first American pope, called for a renewed commitment to peace on Sunday as he marked the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 attacks on his home country.

The Chicago-born pope made his first public comments to commemorate the anniversary, speaking in English at the end of his traditional Sunday noon blessing from his studio window overlooking St. Peter’s Square.

“Two days ago marked the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks in the United States of America,” Leo said. “I renew my prayers for those who lost their lives and for those who continue to bear the wounds of that tragic day.”

He added that “at a time when conflict and violence afflict so many of our brothers and sisters, I invite everyone to pray that the Lord will bestow his gift of peace upon the world.”

Speaking in Italian he added: “The memory of the tragic events of 25 years ago pushes us to renew our commitment to peace, above all with prayer.”

On Sept. 11, 2001, the former Robert Prevost was in Rome attending a big assembly of his Augustinian religious order. At the time, he was the Chicago provincial leader of the Augustinians. Prevost was elected superior of the entire order on Sept. 14, his birthday, a position he held for two consecutive terms until 2012.

Vatican News on Sunday republished excerpts of his first homily as superior, delivered on Sept. 21, 2001. In it, the future American pope reflected on the attacks.

“We cannot fail to remember the tragic events that shook the United States on Sept. 11,” he said in his homily. “The violence that the world witnessed last week in the United States is a tragic expression of a series of problems that are becoming increasingly acute everywhere.

"Hatred and violence will continue to grow as long as so many people are forced to live in extreme poverty and are oppressed by so many forms of injustice.”

Andy Burnham could slash up to £200 off energy bills when Britons can expect a surge in gas and fuel prices this winter due to the Iran war.

Ofgem’s energy price cap will rise by four per cent in October, due to an increase in wholesale gas prices as a result of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which has pushed up the cost of supplying energy in the UK.

This means the annual figure will rise from £1,663 to £1,723 – equivalent to around £5 more per month, or £60 per year, but analysts are already predicting a bigger hike to the price cap in the new year.

The prime minister, who has repeatedly claimed that he hopes to ease the cost of living, is reportedly exploring options to subsidise the millions of households living in fuel poverty, including those who do not currently qualify for existing support.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham has promised to ease the cost of living for Britons ( PA )

A support scheme called the Energy Price Protection Payment (EPPP) could be implemented in January, The Telegraph has reported, which would aim to mitigate the impact of the rising prices.

The paper reported that the EPPP would apply to recipients of the warm homes discount, as well as others deemed in need of support.

Claimants would have to receive benefits, according to the paper, but it remained unclear whether it would cover the estimated additional 2.5 million households classed as being in fuel poverty.

No final decision has reportedly been made on how much the EPPP support would be worth, or whether to proceed with it.

A government spokesperson did not deny the reports but emphasised the VAT cut on electricity bills already being implemented, which is expected to take around £45 off the Ofgem price cap from October, as well as the £150 removed from bills in April.

They said: “The chancellor is fully focused on giving families and businesses breathing space and helping ease cost pressures.

“That’s why we have removed VAT from electricity bills and are reducing electricity costs by up to 25 per cent for more than 10,000 manufacturing businesses through our British industrial competitiveness scheme.”

The government has also expanded the £150 warm home discount to around six million households, extending the scheme for the rest of the decade.

Neil Kenward, Ofgem’s director general for markets, said: “High international gas prices are continuing to drive energy costs in the UK. We welcome the government’s intervention to remove VAT from electricity bills, without which customers would have faced even higher costs this winter.

“Savings are available by choosing a fixed tariff, which are available at £100 or more below the October price cap, and many suppliers offer tariffs with cheaper electricity to smart meter customers for electricity consumed out of peak times.

“It's also worth considering different payment methods, with prepayment customers paying the lowest price cap rates, and could save consumers an average of about £45 compared to direct debit.”

Celine Dion was brought to tears on stage during her emotional comeback concert in Paris, telling fans she had kept her pledge to return following major health struggles.

The French-Canadian singer, 58, kicked off her residency at the Plenitude arena in La Défense on Saturday (12 September), marking her first full-length show in nearly six years.

Dion’s break from performing came in 2022, when she revealed that she had been diagnosed with stiff person syndrome (SPS) diagnosis and cancelled her Courage world tour.

According to the NHS, the rare autoimmune disorder is a neurological condition that causes progressive muscular stiffness and spasms, and has no cure.

open image in gallery Canadian singer Celine Dion reacts as she performs during her first concert ( AFP/Getty )

On stage on Saturday, the five-time Grammy winner was filmed crying during her emotional return to the stage before delivering a speech to tens of thousands of fans in the crowd.

“It’s amazing we are all together,” Dion addressed the cheering audience.

“I made a promise; I made a promise to come back and to be back on stage. Here I am singing for you, and singing for me. Thank you so very much for your support, your patience. I am everything I am because you love me.”

Dion wore a simple, floor-length strapless black gown and accessorised with an ornate silver choker necklace, with her blonde hair in a slicked-back style.

Popular demand recently led the star to extend her ongoing Paris residency to 16 concerts, with further shows scheduled until 14 October.

open image in gallery ( AFP/Getty )

The “My Heart Will Go On” singer had previously cancelled a Las Vegas residency owing to health concerns in 2021, revealing her diagnosis the following year.

Dion paused performing until 2024, when she made a brief appearance singing at the Paris Olympics opening ceremony, and has repeatedly expressed her desire to return to the stage.

Her return was revealed on her birthday on 30 March via an Instagram post, alongside videos displayed beneath the lights of the Eiffel Tower.

Best known for tracks including “Think Twice” and “It’s All Coming Back To Me Now”, the singer will perform her popular hits in both French and English.

News.title: Tora Bora’s last midwife struggles under Taliban rule as aid runs dry
News.content:
The small clinic, crowded with pregnant women, sits in the shadow of Tora Bora in eastern Afghanistan. Twenty-five years ago, those mountains commanded the attention of the world’s most powerful military. Roughly 15 miles from the clinic, in the Tora Bora cave complex, Osama bin Laden was believed to be hiding as American bombs rained down in the hunt for the architect of 9/11.

Today, another consequence of the West’s long entanglement with Afghanistan is playing out beneath those same mountains – in the struggle to keep mothers and babies alive.

In the baking courtyard of Gandab Kharoti health centre, dozens of women enveloped in sapphire blue burqas sit shoulder to shoulder beneath trees waiting to see Shila Ibrahimi, a 27-year-old midwife.

The women rest against walls, dusty, barefoot children play, and mothers cradle sick babies beneath folds of cloth. Some have walked for hours through the mountains to reach her.

Among them is Fawzia, 30, seven-and-a-half months pregnant with her seventh child. Suffering from headaches, she has walked for miles through the heat.

Her husband works far from the village, so she makes the journey with her children and mother-in-law, hoping the Taliban do not stop her for the “crime” of travelling without a male escort.

Under the Taliban’s morality rules, women face restrictions on travelling alone, while UN monitors have documented the regime’s morality inspectors ordering some health facilities not to treat unaccompanied women.

But enforcement varies and Fawzia says nobody challenged her on her journey here. Asked where she would give birth if the clinic closed she says: “We have nowhere else to go. We cannot afford that. We are poor.”

News.title: Springboks look like World Cup champions elect… again
News.content:
In doing so, Erasmus while still relying on his veteran performers, managed to expose some of the next generation to invaluable white heat pressure, including Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, Morne van den Berg and Cameron Hanekom, who all look to the manor born.

And the substance of the series victory is heightened by the fact it came against a regenerated and rejuvenated All Blacks side, who rediscovered their high-octane and relentless attacking identity under new coach Dave Rennie. At times the handling and precision of the All Blacks were so sumptuous that it felt like they might be in a position to level the series in Baltimore.

But the narrative of the previous two Tests continued. At key moments they were let down by their discipline and turnovers in attack to gift the Springboks’ transition ball, and their directness, backed by their power both in collisions and set piece enabled them to pick up points much more easily than their opponents.

At the end, the scoreboard ran away from the All Blacks, which was harsh on them. But one had wondered if they would be able to maintain their intensity at the end of the first half, when it took 32 phases for Will Jordan to score a try to cut the deficit to three points.

News.title: Sabalenka smashes racket and swears at cameraman after Rybakina clinches US Open
News.content:
Sabalenka and Rybankina have now played four slam finals, with the spoils evenly shared after this 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 grapple in the Apple – as a boxing promoter might have referred to it.

There is certainly something pugilistic about the way these two go toe-to-toe. The emphasis is on landing the first blow, so the rallies tend not to be particularly long: only four points out of 193 went beyond nine shots. But the precision of the ball-striking was breathtaking. At one point in the first set, Rybakina had hit eight winners to just a single unforced error – the sort of ratio to send coaches starry-eyed.

Sabalanka arrived on court in her showy jewellery – which is worth more than £300,000 for the full set, according to the manufacturers – and an orange Nike dress that put one in mind of the Dutch national football team. “Total tennis” may have been the goal, but sometimes your opponent doesn’t allow you to play. This was the case in the early stages as Rybakina – whose own yellow-and-black outfit evoked the natural warning signs of a wasp or hornet – seemed to flush every ball right out of the centre of her racket.

Sabalenka actually did a sterling job of digging herself out of trouble in her service games, saving four of five break points in the first set. But this still wasn’t enough, given that Rybakina was defending her own serve with the same serenity that characterises everything she does.

News.title: Former Geordie Guimaraes taunts Sunderland fans as Arsenal show mark of champions
News.content:
Hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

There’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

“I love those challenges,” said Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”

Arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

Kick off 8pm.

News.title: £329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on new players really does take some doing.

“Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

For Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he said. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”

News.title: Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players
News.content:
Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

News.title: Lando Norris on pole for Spanish GP but adds voice to critics of ‘Madring’
News.content:
Red Bull’s Max Verstappen predicted that overtaking would be “practically impossible” in the race. “[The Madring] has a tendency of maybe creating some big shunts in some places,” the Dutchman said. “It reminds me a little bit of Jeddah in a way – fast corners and the walls being very close.

“The only thing that’s already a bit disappointing is that many of the braking zones are angled. This means it’s practically impossible to attack a competitor because you’re braking and simultaneously turning right or left. And that’s the worst thing you can do if you want to create an overtaking opportunity.”

Norris agreed with Verstappen that it would be very difficult to overtake, although that is no bad thing for him provided he can hang on to the lead at the start.

The Briton, though, described the decision to build what is now the longest pit lane on the F1 calendar as a big disappointment.

“I think it has a lot of potential,” Norris said of the Madring. “Just certain things need to be improved. Like the pit lane, which is like six kilometres long. It’s the longest pit lane of the year and the biggest pit loss of the year [in terms of the time it will take to pit – an estimated 25 seconds]. So that just makes overtaking worse. Not overtaking, but it makes the desire to box and do different strategies worse.

“You know, if we’re going to build a new track and spend so much money in building a new track, this is probably one of the main factors, I would say, is you have a short pit lane so people can pit and you then create overtaking.”

Norris described his pole lap as “one of the best laps of his career” and his team principal Andrea Stella fully agreed, describing it as “a masterpiece”.

News.title: Bomb squad rescues rusty Red Roses
News.content:
Mia Venner, Sadia Kabeya, Lucy Packer and Claudia Moloney-MacDonald went over for further tries to add to player-of-the-match Abi Burton’s first-half score.

Moloney-MacDonald’s try wide out on the left was a show-stopper for the crowd of 9,251 in the North West and demonstrated that England have style to go with solidity. But it was the power game that did for Australia.

The Wallaroos scored tries of their own through Faliki Pohiva and Eva Karpani but spent the vast majority of the game manning the defensive barricades. They did so admirably for 40 minutes but when the dam wall blew it blew spectacularly.

They did not help themselves with sin-binnings in either half for Samantha Wood and Karpani, but over 80 minutes the odds will always be stacked in favour of the full-time side against the part-timers.

“The reality is that even at our best we’re probably not good enough. We will be,” said Tim Walsh, Rugby Australia’s director of women’s high performance. “We need an environment where they can concentrate on being full-time athletes. That’s the vision Rugby Australia have and that’s where we’re headed.”

The game was England’s first with the smaller ball being trialled in the women’s game by World Rugby and they only converted four of their eight tries, a statistic which may be seized upon by those who do not care for it. A rugby pitch is not a sterile laboratory though and the swirling, blustery conditions should be taken into account in any dissection of its value.

Ugly scenes took over yesterday’s Tweede Divisie clash – the Dutch third tier – between IJsselmeervogels and G.V.V.V.

Sports.title: ‘Unacceptable’ – Mikel Arteta launches furious rant about referee decisions that ‘can change the course of the season’

MIKEL ARTETA raged at referee John Brooks after Arsenal’s 2-0 win at Sunderland.

The Gunners withstood plenty of pressure from the Black Cats to come away from the Stadium of Light with all three points.



Sunderland spurned a golden chance to take the lead on 56 minutes, when David Raya saved Enzo Le Fee’s penalty.

Bruno Guimaraes fired Arsenal into the lead barely two minutes later, with Bukayo Saka converting from the spot late on to double his side’s advantage.



Despite watching his side triumph, Arteta, 44, was furious with Brooks’ decision to award Sunderland a penalty.

The official blew for a spot kick after watching Ezri Konsa wrestle Dan Ballard to the ground during a long throw routine.

Speaking to TNT Sports after the match, Arteta raged: “It’s unacceptable, at this level it can change the course of the season, the championship.

“I’ve seen it ten times over to be sure. When I saw it live, I thought it’s not possible. It cannot happen.

“The 27 years I’ve been in football, it’s not a penalty in any case, in any context, at any level, in any league.”

Arteta continued his rant when speaking to the BBC, later telling Match of the Day: “We had really good periods but didn’t score and after that they can suffocate you especially when they decided to be really physical and very direct and we had to overcome a situation that in my opinion was absolutely unacceptable at this level.

Sports.title: Andy Cole reveals key Man Utd advantage as he backs them to beat Man City in derby after playing for BOTH sides
Sports.content:
RUTHLESS ANDY COLE helped ruin old club Manchester United’s title dreams on his return to Old Trafford as a City player.

But the former goal machine is backing the Reds to be the ones celebrating later.



Cole achieved legendary status as part of Sir Alex Ferguson’s treble-winning United team in 1999.

His 121 goals in 275 appearances for the Red Devils still has supporters regularly singing his name – though the song has been adapted to Benjamin Sesko of late.



Though 22 years ago he risked destroying that legacy when crossing the divide following stints at Blackburn and Fulham to sign for City.

Despite it being pre-Qatari takeover times, he and the noisy neighbours still proved to be a nuisance for Fergie’s boys.



Cole helped City take four points off their rivals that season – results that proved crucial as United failed to wrestle the title back from Jose Mourinho’s Chelsea.

Even though his prime years were spent there, Cole showed no mercy as he returned to the Theatre of Dreams wearing sky blue. After playing his part in Joey Barton’s late equaliser, only a stunning late Edwin van der Sar save stopped him from sealing City a famous 2-1 win.

Recalling his feelings about stepping out on his old stomping ground in the colours of United’s fierce foes, Cole exclusively told Sun Sport via Unibet Casino: “I’ve been asked this so many times.

“I look at it this way. Ultimately, if you’re moving job, or moving between anything, I don’t know, from Microsoft to Apple, it’s the same thing, isn’t it?



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“You’re still doing your job to the best of your ability. I know people look into it really deeply.

“Obviously, I played for Man United. When I joined Man City, I was just going to play for Man City. Nothing more. I played for Blackburn, then I played for Burnley. I played for Sunderland and I played for Newcastle. It’s no different than moving from Microsoft to Apple.

“It’s simple. I’d like to believe throughout my career I’m very professional. That’s why I’ve ended up with the respect I get from the Manchester United fans or Manchester City fans or Blackburn and Newcastle fans, whatever it is. You’ve just got to be professional in what you do.



“If you’re a professional, then you’re a professional, wherever you are. Being professional, you’ve just got to do to the best of your ability.”

Cole was a thorn in Fergie’s side once again the following January when helping City take derby bragging rights with a 3-1 win in the return fixture at the Etihad.

The result was a bitter blow to United’s title aspirations, eventually finishing eight points behind Chelsea.

And even though United still remain deep in his heart, the 54-year-old still has no regrets.

He said: “It was going up against former team-mates who I spent a lot of time with, who I played with for many years.



“I want to try and win any game against whatever team it was. Maybe that’s just me.

“So when I moved to Manchester City. It was my job to score goals for Manchester City. When you move job you still try to get the best out of yourself. That’s what I did.

“I’ve always been that kind of individual. I give everything I’ve got. So even though it felt a little bit different, a little bit strange, I’ve got to be professional in my job.

“No one really even talks about me going to Manchester City or anything like that. And because of what I am as a person, as a human being, I’ll go anywhere and give 100 per cent. It’s that simple.”



These days Erling Haaland is the undoubted goal king of Manchester. He has eight derby goals and found the target five times already this term.

Sports.title: Newcastle legend Andy Cole says Anthony Elanga is putting ‘nonsense’ flop talk behind him under Matthias Jaissle
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE legend Andy Cole says Anthony Elanga is putting the “nonsense” talk of him being a flop behind him.

The Swedish winger, 24, was a huge disappointment last term after Eddie Howe forked out £55m to Nottingham Forest to make him the club’s third most-expensive signing.



A return of no goals and a single assist in the Premier League failed to impress the Toon Army and piled even more pressure on Howe as the Mags slumped to a 12th place finish.

Elanga, however, has made a blistering start under new boss Matthias Jaissle with goals in the German’s first two top-flight matches.



He missed out on becoming the first Newcastle player since Cole in 1993 to score in the opening three Prem games of the season in last week’s 2-2 draw with Bournemouth.

But Cole, who bagged 68 times in 84 games wearing Black and White, told the reborn star to just “keep his head” as he looks to return to the goal trail at Elland Road on Monday.



Speaking exclusively to Sun Sport via Unibet Casino, the former striker said: “Anthony is a very good player. It was a big move last season from Nottingham Forest to Newcastle.

“He’ll be honest himself and most probably say it didn’t go the way he would have wanted it to go. But he’s hit the ground running this season, which is the most important thing.

“He’s just got to keep his head down, keep performing, and then all the nonsense that was spoken about him last season, everyone will be telling him how good he is and slapping him on the back. That’s football.”

Cole scored for Newcastle home and away against Leeds in an epic 1993/94 campaign that produced 41 goals for the hitman. And his strike to earn a point in a 1-1 draw at Elland Road in April was critical to helping Kevin Keegan’s side achieve a third-placed finish.

Sports.title: Britain’s first £1million teenager who faced David Beckham is now Man Utd scout and runs a church
Sports.content:
HE was British football’s first £1million teenager 32 years ago, but now Bruce Dyer is dedicated to finding kids who can follow his pathway into the game.

It was back in 1994 that ­Crystal Palace paid Watford the seven-figure sum for the then 18-year-old.



The 51-year former striker now works as a regional scout for Manchester United, but also coaches in schools promoting his approach to the sport.

Based in Yorkshire, he said: “When I am working with youngsters in academies and schools I would like to think that I am the absolute example of what any kid can achieve.



“I was just a lad from East London with this dream of playing football.

“It does seem crazy that it’s over three decades since Palace signed me for £1million when I was 18 after I had only made my senior debut for Watford a year earlier.

“I look back to that time and I seriously have to pinch myself.

“It was a crazy, whirlwind period of my life.

“I joined Watford’s youth system at 15, was recommended by the club’s kit manager, Ken Brooks, and made my debut for the Hornets when I was 17.”

One of Dyer’s ­earliest football memories is playing in the East End of London at grassroots level for a team called Grasshoppers.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Their rivals were a side called Ridgeway Rovers who had a youngster called David Beckham playing for them.

It was a special football ­education which served Dyer well throughout his 15 years as a player at 11 clubs between 1993 and 2008.

One of the highlights of his career was finishing top scorer for the England Under-21s when they won the Toulon Tournament in 1994, netting in the final as the Three Lions beat Portugal 2-0 — a side that included Sol Campbell, Trevor Sinclair and Jamie Redknapp.

He added: “I loved every ­minute of it.



“Now I would like to think it’s my vocation in my working life to help other kids have that pinch-me moment and achieve the dream I enjoyed.”

Dyer accepts the opportunities for aspiring stars to play at Premier League level are ­statistically slim.

He said: “You have to look beyond that as a youngster starting out in the game today.

“I am a true believer that my dream came true to play at the top level and so it can happen for anyone else I coach or scout.”

For the last eight years the ex-goal-getter has run Love Life Church UK in Barnsley, which he founded in 2018, having turned to religion for guidance at the start of the century.



But Dyer has also enjoyed two huge additional reflected glories over the last few years — one in the game and one in his personal life.

First his wife, Janine, appeared on TV shows The Voice and Britain’s Got Talent — wowing the judges and audience — something Dyer says has brought him more joy than his own football career.

He said: “I am blessed to have had Janine as my soul mate.

“Her career was put on hold while she was having children, but she has this talent, I am so pleased she has been able to share.”

Janine is the founder and director of the Sheffield Community Gospel Choir and is a multi-award-winning, gifted singer.



And on a football level, he has watched with pride as his old side ­Palace — where he netted 44 goals in 164 games over four years in the mid-Nineties — have lifted the FA Cup, Community Shield and European Conference League silverware over the last 16 months.

He added: “When I was at Palace they were known as a yo-yo club, jumping up and down between the ­Premier League and second tier. It’s on a different scale today.

“I couldn’t be happier for supporters, too — they have an incredible fanbase. Now they are into the Europa League this season and I hope they go from strength to strength.

“Dougie Freedman invited me back to Palace a couple of years ago and I did a talk with the Under-18s.

“I was absolutely blown away by how much the facilities had changed at the club from when I was there. Palace will always have a very special place in my heart.”

Sports.title: Benjamin Sesko claims he is in ‘perfect’ condition at Man Utd and reveals why he loves the city so much
Sports.content:
BENJAMIN SESKO insists he is in a “perfect” condition following his return for Manchester United.

Sesko scored his second goal in as many games on his first start in more than four months in United’s 4-0 Champions League victory against Sabah on Thursday.



The 22-year-old striker missed all six of United’s pre-season friendlies as the club carefully managed his recovery from a shin injury.

SunSport revealed in May that United did not risk Sesko in their final three matches last term to allow his shin to sufficiently heal.



During his lay-off, Sesko gained extra muscle mass and he is vying for a first Premier League start of the campaign against Manchester City on Sunday.

Sesko only managed two goals in his first five months after a £73.68million transfer from RB Leipzig, but he has scored 12 goals in 20 games this calendar year.



Sesko is now adamant he is in the best possible physical and mental state, 13 months on from his move to United.

“We just need a little bit longer than usual,” he said of his injury. “Because if you start too early, it might appear again.

“And I think waiting a little bit longer was a great decision, and now it’s healed, so it’s perfect.

“Obviously, I had quite some time from the injury to gain some muscle. I lost a lot (of mobility) because I was overweight with muscles and I couldn’t really move so much.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“But now I feel very good and I think I’m in the right place at the moment.”

When asked how his frame of mind is now he is into his second season at United, Sesko replied: “Way better, especially than last season.

“I changed a country. Everything was new for me. Now for me it’s like I’m really enjoying it.

“I’m really happy here. I love life here. I have team-mates that are perfect.

“I can’t really complain about anything.



“What do I love? Just the vibes. I like to go to the city for a walk. I can do certain arcade things that I like to do in my free time.

“Then obviously spending a little time with the players. And I think it’s just what I like.”

Sesko stressed he is still “far” from emulating some of United’s greatest strikers. Robin van Persie was the last United frontman to hit the 30-goal barrier in a season back in 2012-13.

Slovenia international Sesko tallied a creditable 12 goals in 32 games last term and will be expected to comfortably surpass that in a campaign that United are guaranteed to have at least ten more matches.



“Obviously, the more games I’m getting, the more comfortable I feel and the more free I feel in the game as well,” Sesko explained.

“For me, the focus is all about scoring goals to provide everything for this club. But then also certain things that sometimes – like link-up play – just this little things that can be all-round.

“I think it will just come now in time. I’m here. I feel better and better every day. This is the most important.”

Sesko did not get off the bench in Michael Carrick’s first match in charge against Manchester City in January but could appreciate the United coach’s instant impact from the substitutes’ bench.

United won 2-0 at Old Trafford in what is widely considered their best performance since the 2024 FA Cup final triumph against City.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Definitely straight away,” Sesko recalled of Carrick’s immediate effect. “Even from the start when he came, it was something special.

“I think everyone felt it.”

Sports.title: Garcia takes out Benn in just two rounds
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia hammered Conor Benn to defeat inside two rounds at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas.

Garcia successfully defended the WBC welterweight championship with a ruthless display of speed, power and precision, ending Benn's world title dream early in their Las Vegas showdown.

Benn was stepping up to a new level in the first world title fight of his career as the UK star attempted to secure what would have been one of British boxing's biggest overseas upsets.

Garcia, though, proved too much.

Benn was fighting below the welterweight limit for the first time in over four years.

Last year, after his provisional suspension for an anti-doping violation was lifted, Benn boxed family rival Chris Eubank Jr twice at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Both of those bouts were up at middleweight, with Benn avenging his loss in the first contest when he dropped and outscored Eubank in the second.

He began moving back down to welterweight after that, meeting Regis Prograis in a catchweight bout, also at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, on the undercard of Tyson Fury's comeback earlier this year.

Image: Garcia drops Benn heavily in the second round.

He completed the challenge of boiling back down in weight but couldn't match Garcia.

In his career Garcia has come up from lighter divisions, but has mixed in exalted company. He recorded a stunning win over Olympic gold medallist Luke Campbell and lost to Gervonta Davis at lightweight. He dominated Devin Haney, although he came in over the super-lightweight limit for that fight. That result was changed to a no contest after Garcia failed a drug test.

After a year-long ban, he lost to Rolando Romero in a Times Square event before getting a shot at then WBC champion Mario Barrios. Garcia dropped Barrios en route to winning a decision and claiming the belt.

Image: Garcia traps Benn on the ropes.

Benn was installed as his mandatory challenger but Garcia showed his calibre early on the fight. At the outset he shook up the Briton with a quick left hook.

At the end of the first round Garcia unleashed hurtful back hands, while Benn tried to club back at him with his right.

In the second round Garcia ripped his right across to drop Benn heavily. The Briton rose unsteadily. He needed to clinch to try to clear his head, but the American pinned him on the end of savage punches.

Garcia tore into him, smashing him into the ropes. He hurt Benn to the body and then battered him round the head, his sheer speed clearly apparent. The referee then stepped between them to end it at 1:25 of the second round.

"I kind of figured he would just come at me crazy," Garcia said.

"Second round, I said I'm tired of him coming forward; I'm going stand my ground a little bit ... and then he got caught with a hellacious one."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jai Opetaia landed a powerful flurry of shots in the ninth round to force a stoppage victory over Noel Mikaelian and accepted the challenge of David Benavidez next. Fight footage courtesy of DAZN.

On the undercard Australia's formidable cruiserweight champion Jai Opetaia continued his unbeaten run, dispatching WBC titlist Noel Mikaelian.

In the ninth round the southpaw cracked Mikaelian with a left hook then an even harder right hook, leaving him stunned on the ropes. The strands held him up so the referee administered a count but Mikaelian could not continue from there and was stopped at 1:30 of the session.

Sports.title: Garcia targets Lopez next | ‘Benn will be back’
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia will look to unify world championships with Teofimo Lopez next after his stunning stoppage victory over Conor Benn.

Garcia looked imperious as he dismissed Benn inside two rounds at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas.

But the American superstar believes Benn can rebuild and recover.

"He just needs to gain a little bit more experience. I don't think he has enough experience at this point. I don't think he was as experienced as me but I think he will be back. He went in, tried to fight me," Garcia said.

"You can't jump in like that. It's not the move. I think that he needs to be a little bit more patient.

"He's an alright dude. I have a new level of respect for him. I hope he can come back and do great things in the sport."

Image: Garcia finishes Benn on the ropes.

After defending the WBC welterweight title, Garcia immediately had words for WBA champion Teofimo Lopez, who was in attendance at the arena.

"I want to unify against Teofimo. I think that's the move," Garcia said afterwards. "It's a huge fight and Teo's an entertaining dude and it's going to be a hell of a build-up and he's a good fighter too so let's run it."

Lopez, who has past wins over Vasiliy Lomachenko and Josh Taylor on his stellar resume, was soundly beaten by Shakur Stevenson earlier this year. But Lopez bounced back to beat Rolando Romero, who himself beat Garcia last year.

But Garcia warned: "I was just getting started in there [against Benn]. There's a lot of things that I've been working on. But that's just another opportunity to show that in another fight.

"I have a lot of weapons in my arsenal that I didn't bring out yet."

Sports.title: England player ratings: Lawrence, Cox, Gay selection headache as all impress
Sports.content:
England clinched a first home series whitewash of Pakistan with an eight-wicket win in the third Test at Edgbaston, but who stood out from Joe Root's side - and who didn't?

Ben Duckett - 3

Batting: 11 and 0

Image: England opener Ben Duckett struggled during the series, scoring a combined 44 runs over his five innings

A Test match to forget for Duckett. In fact, it has been a pretty miserable series as a whole, with his first-innings 17 at Lord's serving as his highest score.

He did, however, notch England's only Test ton of the summer against New Zealand at Trent Bridge, so his place at the top of the order isn't under threat - at least for now...

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ben Duckett hit the only England Test century this summer against New Zealand at Trent Bridge in June

He was also a bit butter-fingered in the slips this week, dropping three chances, albeit his two put down in the first innings didn't prove too costly as Pakistan were still bundled out for 133 in only 33.5 overs.

Emilio Gay - 6

Batting: 60 and 0

It has been a bit of a back-and-forth affair with regards to Gay's place in the starting Test side going forward, with the Durham left-hander seemingly locking up his spot with another battling half-century in the first innings - his third such score this summer.

But then his second-innings duck has somewhat opened up the debate again, especially given the performance of others who could end up elbowing him out of the way when the currently injured Jacob Bethell likely returns to the team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England's start to day four could not have gone worse after Mohammad Abbas removed Ben Duckett and Emilio Gay in the first over

It was, admittedly, a terrific delivery from Mohammad Abbas that ensured he wouldn't trouble the scorers in the second innings, but it's precisely why he'll be kicking himself with how he got out first time round - dragging a wide one from Razaullah back onto his stumps - when a first Test hundred was there for the taking.

Jordan Cox - 7

Batting: 4 and 59no

Much like Gay, Cox's fortunes and future prospects see-sawed a touch over the course of this Test, as he copped a low one in the first innings - also falling foul of Abbas, lbw - but his calm, unbeaten half-century alongside the skipper on the fourth morning saw England to victory from a positon of peril at 2-2.

Image: Jordan Cox scored 59 hugely valuable runs as part of an unbroken 128-run partnership with Joe Root that took England to victory at Edgbaston

It will have been hard for Joe Root not to have taken note of that, as he looks for the right sort of characters to take this side forward. And Cox seems to have character in spades.

That was also evident with his keeping, when deputising impressively for Jamie Smith, who sat out the second innings with an injured thumb. He claimed four terrific catches and a stumping to finally end Razaullah's extraordinary knock.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jordan Cox took a superb catch to dismiss Babar Azam in the second innings at Edgbaston

Joe Root - 7

Batting: 8 and 62no

Just when England needed a captain's innings, Root duly obliged, his unbeaten half-century on the fourth morning - just his third of a barren summer by his standards - allaying any fears of a catastrophic late collapse to defeat.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day four of the third Test between England and Pakistan at Edgbaston as Joe Root steered his side to victory

Instead, he celebrates a series sweep - England's first at home over Pakistan - on his return as permanent Test captain, though his lbw issues persist after Razaullah was the one to pin him in the first innings, in spectacular fashion with only his fourth ball in Test cricket. It takes Root's tally to eight such dismissals from his 10 Test innings' this summer.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player 21-year-old debutant Razaullah took the wicket of England's all-time leading Test run-scorer Joe Root with only his fourth ball

Also, he moved one clear of Australia's Steve Smith and onto 220 in their personal battle to claim the record number of catches by an outfielder in Test cricket.

Harry Brook - 7

Batting: 75

Brook will be another kicking himself for missing out on a hundred in the first innings, with one seemingly at his mercy before he needlessly ran himself out on the second morning.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Brook spurned his chance of making a century in the first innings as he ran himself out on 75

He's been England's most consistent batter in the testing conditions served up this summer, with this his fifth half-century, while he has had starts of at least 20 in all but two of his innings.

It will make him all the more frustrated at the fact that a century has eluded him, but he has shown greater responsibility with the bat - certainly against Pakistan - which is encouraging after fans began growing tired of his, at times, reckless approach in the Bazball era.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player We take a look back at an extraordinary summer of Test series which saw Ben Stokes retire, a new England captain, the end of Bazball, and a series sweep of Pakistan.

Dan Lawrence - 8

Batting: 65

Bowling: 2-17

Player of the match. With Ollie Robinson denied for the first time in a Test he's played this summer.

Lawrence is another vying for a regular place in this side and he's certainly done his chances no harm, with bat, ball and in the field.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dan Lawrence produced a stunning catch at slip off Gus Atkinson to dismiss Shan Masood for 95, denying the Pakistan batter a century at Edgbaston

His standout contribution was a spectacular catch in the slips - one-handed, diving low to his right - to see off Shan Masood five shy of a century. But he also grabbed two wickets in his 4.4 second-innings overs, including Azan Awais (59) to end his 125-run third-wicket stand with Masood and finally the wicket of Razaullah to end day three.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dan Lawrence claimed England’s first wicket of day three as Azan Awais fell for 59 following a successful Joe Root review and sharp catch from Jordan Cox

If anything his off-spin was under-used, with that being a key string to his bow to support England's preference for a four-pronged pace attack looking ahead to the winter tour of South Africa and next summer's Ashes.

With the bat, like Gay and Brook before him, he'll rue missing out on a first-innings ton when dragging a rather innocuous delivery from Mohammad Imran back onto his stumps.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dan Lawrence couldn't hide his fury after chopping one back onto his stumps when eyeing up a maiden Test century

Jamie Smith - 7

Batting: 69

The forgotten man in this Test, with his involvement ended two days in, as a blow to the finger when stood up to the stumps on day one prevented him from donning the gloves in the second innings.

It looks a precautionary measure more than anything, with it not keeping him from batting on day two as he again impressed with a typically brisk 69 before chipping one back to Razaullah off his own bowling.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A fired-up Razaullah celebrated wildly as caught and bowled Jamie Smith

While Cox impressed in his absence, Smith has also barely put a foot wrong behind the stumps all summer, so he'll likely still start if fit for South Africa.

Gus Atkinson - 6

Bowling: 0-31 and 3-109

Batting: 19

It's been tough sledding for Atkinson this series, with only one wicket to show for his efforts prior to the second innings - as the rest of the pace quartet profited.

He has bowled better than his numbers would suggest, often coming on as second change, sidelined as others wreaked havoc with the new ball and when bowling to the tail.

Image: Gus Atkinson claimed three second-innings wickets after having only taken one through the first two and a half Tests

But Root showed faith in his fast bowler after lunch on day three, with Pakistan 184-3 in their second innings, letting him loose for an eight-over spell that was his best yet and brought with it the wicket of Masood - as much as he owed a debt of gratitude to Lawrence too.

He'd later add Ghazi Ghori and Imran before he too couldn't escape punishment from the blade of Razaullah.

Ollie Robinson - 8

Bowling: 3-15 and 2-54

Batting: 50

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ollie Robinson took two wickets for no runs in the opening over of Pakistan’s second innings in the third Test against England

Robinson was at it yet again with the new ball, dismissing Saim Ayub and Abdullah Shafique in his opening spell in both innings, needing only four deliveries to see the back of them second time round - the former out for a pair upon his sudden, surprise call up to the touring side in between Tests that did him no favours.

Robinson's wicket of Saim in the first innings was his 100th in Test cricket, while his double strike in the first over of the second took his tally for the series to 21 at an average of 6.66 a pop, which grew to just the 8.76 apiece upon Pakistan's battling display on day three.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ollie Robinson claimed his 100th Test wicket with his first-innings dismissal of Saim Ayub

In all seriousness, his effectiveness does diminish when taken deep into later spells, which could be a concern on flatter decks if that's what awaits in South Africa or next year's Ashes, but it's extremely hard to pick fault given just how impressive his reintroduction to the side has been this summer.

Also pitched in with the bat, scoring his second Test fifty.

Jofra Archer - 6

Bowling: 3-25 and 1-120

Batting: 32no

Image: Jofra Archer has taken 23 wickets at an average of 24.82 apiece over the five Tests he's played this summer

Not his best showing, with at least one of his three first-innings wickets a real gift from Masood, spooned straight to midwicket.

His dismissal of Saud Shakeel to a brute of a short ball in the second gave nod to him at his best, but he was one of several England bowlers to lose the plot late on the third evening as Razaullah smacked them to all parts.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Razaullah smashed NINE sixes to equal Tim Southee’s record for the most by a player on Test debut during a remarkable innings against England at Edgbaston

Still, an encouraging summer on the whole, with five consecutive Tests for the previously injury-plagued pacer a real tick for England.

Josh Tongue - 7

Bowling: 4-42 and 2-106

Batting: 15

Trademark Tongue in the first innings, with three of his four wickets scattering the stumps - the top of Babar's off peg knocked back with the fast bowler's dream delivery, Imran undone by a toe-crushing yorker and Shakeel seen off by a devastating nip-backer.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Josh Tongue led the way with the ball for England in the first innings, with three of his four dismissals clean-bowled!

He was expensive in the second innings, going at more than six an over, until his and Archer's bouncer theory proved incisive - until Razaullah arrived at the middle, that is - as Tongue got Babar to glove one behind.

Sports.title: Furious Arteta rages over 'unacceptable' Sunderland penalty call
Sports.content:
A furious Mikel Arteta described Sunderland's penalty in Arsenal's 2-0 win at the Stadium of Light as "unacceptable".

The home side were awarded a spot kick in the 54th minute when defender Ezri Konsa was adjudged to have held Sunderland's Dan Ballard by referee John Brooks.

"The referee's call of penalty to Sunderland for a holding offence by Konsa on Ballard was checked and confirmed by VAR," said a statement published by the Premier League Match Centre.

The statement continued by quoting the interaction between on-pitch referee Brooks and the VAR.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League clash between Sunderland and Arsenal

"REF: 'He's all over him at the near post facing the wrong way.' VAR: 'I'm happy that it's a holding offence. The foul is confirmed. Confirming the on-field decision of penalty.'"

David Raya saved Enzo Le Fee's spot kick and Bruno Guimaraes scored Arsenal's opening goal just 121 seconds later but Arteta vented his anger at the decision despite the result.

"The first question we have to discuss is this," he said at the start of his press conference. "This is not acceptable at this level.

"It was a beautiful game of football with two teams, with an atmosphere in the stadium that was unbelievable.

"Sunderland are so well organised, they are so good in so many phases, they have great players and they create a lot of issues. We have to cope with all of that in a really difficult week.

"And on top of that, we have to go through what we have done today, that, in my opinion, is not acceptable.

"I watched it 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how they think to give a penalty in that situation, or the way the VAR has to intervene.

"So I don't know what to think.

Image: David Raya superbly saved Enzo Le Fee's penalty at 0-0

"I'm sad that we have to discuss this after such a beautiful game, that at this level, has the gravity of that. Because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship.

"At this level, with all the work we put in, this cannot happen."

Arsenal's victory was wrapped up by a late Bukayo Saka penalty but Arteta, who was booked for going out of his technical area earlier in the game, was similarly angry in his post-match interview with TNT Sports, describing the incident as a "judo roll".

"It's not a penalty in any case, in any context, in any league," he added.

Sports.content:
Meanwhile, Jayde Riviere and Emma Watson are absent from the Manchester United squad.

Melvine Malard is not available to face her former club today after suffering a knock in training. The Blues are also without Mayra Ramirez and Manaka Matsukubo.

Hello and welcome to coverage of the WSL meeting between Manchester United and Chelsea. Both teams dropped points in their opening games last weekend, with United suffering a 2-1 loss to London City Lionesses and Chelsea held to a 1-1 draw by Aston Villa at Stamford Bridge.

Today presents a completely different challenge. The Blues have won five of their last six games against United, with the remaining fixture resulting in a draw.

However, given it’s just the start of a new campaign, anything can happen.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta says penalty given to Sunderland ‘unacceptable at this level’
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta’s delight at Arsenal’s latest win was tempered by his fury with the referee John Brooks as the champions triumphed 2-0 at Sunderland on Saturday night.

Before Bruno Guimarães gave Arsenal the lead in a tight match that Régis Le Bris’s team were arguably unlucky to lose, David Raya made a brilliant save to deny Enzo Le Fée from the penalty spot. Arteta, however, did not believe that Ezri Konsa had hauled Dan Ballard to the ground, instead blaming the Sunderland man for pulling down his opponent.

“We had to overcome a really tough opponent in a difficult place,” said Arsenal’s manager. “Sunderland can suffocate you and they decided to be really physical and very direct and we also had to overcome a situation that, in my opinion was unacceptable at this level.

“I’m very worried and sad because this can never be a penalty. It’s a judo roll from the opponent. Ezri does nothing. We have to take responsibility to protect the game. Today the game was unprotected and it could have cost us the win and our momentum. I’m really sad. It should never have happened.”

Arteta, who was booked in the first half for persistently stepping out of his technical area, hailed Guimarães’s goal as “beautiful” after watching Bukayo Saka scored a second goal from the penalty spot in stoppage time, when Sunderland’s Reinildo was sent off for a second bookable offence.

Le Bris was left with mixed feelings. “I’m proud and disappointed, these are the two words that are in my mind at the minute,” said Sunderland’s manager. “I’m proud because I think we showed that we are really close to achieving something big against one of the best teams in Europe right now. After the first half we were a bit reserved with the ball I think, but our second half was excellent.

“We got the momentum, created chances and it was a big save from Raya from the penalty. I think it was very good goalkeeping rather than a poor penalty. Raya was absolutely impressive today.

“We stayed in the game and we created other chances but we didn’t score and that was the difference today.

Sports.title: De Zerbi says Spurs have ‘mental block’ after wait for league win continues
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi says his Tottenham players continue to lack physical fitness and must “unblock” themselves in psychological terms after they drew their latest Premier League blank in a home 0-0 with Everton. It is now four games in the competition since the start of the season without a goal for Spurs; they sit 17th in the table with two points and were booed off by frustrated fans.

De Zerbi gave a number of explanations for Spurs’ slow start, chief among them the injuries that a clutch of players sustained on the long-haul pre-season tour to New Zealand and Australia. He lamented the impact of the World Cup on the return dates of certain players and mentioned how Sávio and Omar Marmoush had signed late in the transfer window.

De Zerbi talked up a positive opening 30 minutes from his players against Everton but accepted they ran out of steam and that there was a psychological problem.

“There is a word in Italian – sbloccarsi – that literally translates as if we unblock ourselves,” De Zerbi said. “[It is] a mental block because four games, no wins, no goals scored … it is tough for the players. The team is extremely strong, we can score goals and we can win games. And then we have to respect the history of the players in their careers. Forget Dominic Solanke and Marmoush – the other players … they didn’t score many, many goals in their careers and we have to find these goals. I think we can do so with the quality of our play.”

De Zerbi warmed to a familiar theme when he went back to the pre-season tour. “I said we started this season late for many, many reasons; too late,” he said. “Many players at the World Cup, many injuries, many problems in Australia. Micky van de Ven suffered an injury in Australia. Domi Solanke the same. James Maddison the same. Mateus Fernandes suffered an injury in Australia. He lost 15 days and it’s not so quick. Sávio and Marmoush, they came 10 days ago. I started to work with this [whole] group not last Thursday but two Thursdays ago. So, I think we have not the right physical condition yet.

Sports.title: Hull stun Chelsea with Mohamed Belloumi double before João Pedro rescues a point
Sports.content:
The chants from the away end about winning the league were sung in jest, but Hull continue to show they are here to stay. Sergej Jakirovic’s dogged, intelligent side are third in the Premier League after extending their unbeaten start to four games and can even count themselves unfortunate not to have beaten another of the Big Six after pushing Chelsea to the limit in an absorbing battle at a frustrated Stamford Bridge.

Hull were 2-1 up at half-time and they had the chances to snatch the points during the second half. It took two big saves from Emiliano Martínez to prevent an upset, but this was not a good day for the Chelsea goalkeeper or his new teammates. He was one of several at fault when Hull, having dusted themselves down after conceding from Morgan Rogers early on, went ahead through Mohamed Belloumi’s quickfire double. The ease with which Chelsea’s advantage was handed over left the normally calm and considered Xabi Alonso accusing his side of being “soft” without the ball.

Alonso craves the comfort of a forgettable win. Chelsea have been exhilarating in attack, but they cannot defend. They are conceding two goals per game and the basketball nature of Alonso’s approach has created chaos rather than control. “It’s all entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win,” he said. “It will take time. When we get the lead you still need to be competing and not to give the chance so easily for them to come back.

“Especially in the first goal, we can do much better. It was too soft to give them hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances, but that changed the mood. We will get better, but it’s having an impact on our performances.”

It is ridiculous that Rogers, Cole Palmer and João Pedro are having to do so much in attack. Chelsea led after seven minutes, surging forward when they left four players forward at a Hull corner. João Pedro’s pass reached Rogers and the £117m signing from Aston Villa drove past Regan Slater before beating Konstantinos Tzolaki at his near post with a low, hard and early shot from the left.

View image in fullscreen João Pedro fires home Chelsea’s equaliser in the second half. Photograph: Andy Rain/EPA

Chelsea should have pushed on after becoming the first side to breach Hull since their promotion. Pedro Neto tested Tzolakis from the right, but the hosts became vague and complacent. This was the first time they have dominated possession in a league game this season and the result was not convincing. Hull limited them to an xG of 0.89, highlighting Chelsea’s issues against low blocks, and were clinical when they attacked.

The soft defending Alonso referenced for the equaliser started with Malo Gusto failing to deal with a long punt from Tzolakis in the 28th minute. Ryan Giles outmuscled the right-back and hooked a cross to the far post. Jorrel Hato misread the Hull left-back’s delivery, leaving Belloumi to rap a shot past Martínez.

Chelsea are without a win against promoted sides in five home games. They do not smell danger, while Alonso’s decision to leave Maxence Lacroix out at centre-back and shift from a back three to a 4-2-3-1 system backfired. Hull had so much space on the flanks. They pushed again and Belloumi’s flick found Lewie Coyle, who ran off Rogers but saw his shot cleared off the line by Levi Colwill.

“The dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it,” Alonso said. “Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”

There was no response from Chelsea after Colwill turned Coyle’s shot wide. A corner came in from the left, Martínez flapped and Semi Ajayi’s header hit the bar. The ball came to Belloumi, whose shot flew in thanks to a deflection.

Alonso reacted at half-time, Hato making way for Pep Chavarría at left-back. Reece James drew a save from Tzolakis with a free-kick but Hull carried a threat on the break. They almost extended their lead when Martínez spilled a shot from Slater.

Martínez redeemed himself, blocking the rebound from McBurnie, and Chelsea soon levelled. Palmer, otherwise quiet, surprised Hull with a direct run. The No 10 drove down the left and picked out João Pedro, who lashed a shot into the roof of the net.

Hull refused to lie down. Ajayi, Giles and John Egan were outstanding at the back and the visitors maintained their shape when losing Nobel Mendy after a nasty collision with João Pedro.

Jakirovic made bold substitutions. Alonso threw Danny Welbeck on. Palmer scooped over from 20 yards and Tzolakis thwarted Rogers, but Hull had the best chance. Giles crossed again and Mohamed-Ali Cho shot straight at Martínez from close range.

Hull settled for a point. Jakirovic quashed talk of qualifying for Europe, insisting that survival remains the aim. The Bosnian has everyone pulling in the same direction. Before the start of the season he told his staff he would give them seven days off if Hull took eight points from their first five games. Mission completed with a game to spare.

Sports.title: Frustrated Liverpool lack any spark as Fulham claim deserved first point
Sports.content:
Álvaro Arbeloa was often the obstacle to Andoni Iraola’s international ambitions back in the days when both were vying for a right-back role with Spain. On his return to Anfield, and under the watchful eye of former manager Rafael Benítez, Arbeloa thwarted Iraola once again to claim his first Premier League point as Fulham head coach against an ineffective Liverpool.

Fulham belied their lowly position and run of three league defeats to take a merited point from a Liverpool team that was a pale imitation of the one that beat Atlético Madrid in the Champions League on Wednesday. Iraola fielded a front four that cost almost £400m but the most impressive forward on display was the Fulham academy graduate Josh King. The draw was Liverpool’s third in four league games under their new head coach and the seventh in 12 Premier League matches at Anfield in 2026. Progress can be painfully slow at times.

“It is the first game we’ve had problems creating chances and making the difference offensively,” Iraola said. “It is easy for me to say the players were tired (after Atlético). There was a lack of freshness and, we cannot hide it, it was the worst turnaround in terms of 60-70 hours. But this is going to happen in the season and we have to adapt. Sometimes you need a set play or a moment of brilliance to win these kind of games but we were not as good offensively as other games.”

Liverpool were sluggish and sloppy – Florian Wirtz and Kostas Tsimikas put simple passes straight out of play in the first half, setting the tone for a disjointed performance – while Fulham bypassed the central midfield pairing of Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch repeatedly. The visitors’ confidence and composure on the ball, along with their defensive organisation, was hugely impressive considering the start to the season under the former Real Madrid interim coach and Liverpool defender. With more conviction in front of goal, Arbeloa’s side could have capitalised on Liverpool’s malaise.

Bradley Barcola created an early, difficult chance for Alexander Isak that the striker swept wide of the far post. Victor Muñoz went closer still with a glancing header from a Szoboszlai corner. Bernd Leno, the Fulham goalkeeper, reacted superbly to claw the ball away. But that was the sum total of Liverpool’s first-half enterprise.

Fulham were gifted a glorious opportunity when Alisson played a ridiculous pass to Gravenberch, who was under pressure from Sander Berge. Berge’s challenge fell to King, who was sent flying by the Liverpool goalkeeper but the referee, Thomas Bramall, played a good advantage as Gonzalo García received the loose ball. García had time to pick his spot but Jérémy Jacquet blocked his shot in front of the goalline.

View image in fullscreen Jérémy Jacquet clears the ball off the line to deny Fulham the lead. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

The visitors prospered down their left and Oscar Bobb missed another good opening when, unmarked and 18 yards out, he miscontrolled Alex Iwobi’s pinpoint delivery. Jacquet came to Liverpool’s rescue once again seconds later when preventing García breaking through with an excellent challenge.

Liverpool were deserving of a few home truths during the break – chiefly, you would have been lambasted for this last season under Arne Slot – and performed with more intensity in the second half. But not with any more threat. The introductions of Cody Gakpo, Alexis Mac Allister and Milos Kerkez brought modest improvement but Fulham continued to contain the hosts comfortably. The new signing David Affengruber had a fine debut and Calvin Bassey was commanding against Isak.
