The Vice President also made a case for migration as an important driver of development, innovation and economic growth, noting that immigrants have historically contributed to the building of nations and cities across the world.

“Nations are built by immigrants. Even cities are built by people who came from outside, not just by the locals. That goes to show that we have so much to gain from global migration,” he explained.

Citing Nigerians in diaspora as an example, Shettima said Nigerians abroad have continued to distinguish themselves through education, enterprise and professional achievement.

“Recent Pew Research Centre analysis of 2024 US Census Bureau data showed that 67 per cent of Nigerian-born Black immigrants aged 25 and above in the United States held at least a bachelor’s degree, the highest proportion among the major Black immigrant groups examined,” he stated.

The vice president also commended Okonjo-Iweala for her leadership of the WTO, urging her to continue deploying her experience in the service of global development.

“You are doing a very wonderful job at the WTO, but you still have a lot to contribute to humanity,” he told the WTO DG.

Okonjo-Iweala, the first woman and first African to head the WTO, began her second four-year term as Director-General in September 2025.

Meanwhile, Shettima will present Nigeria’s partnership and foreign investment opportunities today when he speaks to leaders of the BRICS alliance at the ongoing summit themed, “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”

While seeking a more inclusive international order, the vice president will reiterate the objective of President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda to create sustainable opportunities for its people through reforms, the expansion of infrastructure, and the promotion of private-sector-led growth.

World.title: Four women found dead: Is a serial killer lurking in Kempton Park?
World.content:
Police have launched a specialised investigation after four women were found dead in Kempton Park, sparking serial killer fears. SAPS has not confirmed that the cases are linked. Image: Pexels

Police have launched a specialised investigation after four women were found dead in Kempton Park over the past two months, sparking fears that a serial killer could be operating in the area.

The South African Police Service (SAPS) said officers discovered the latest victim on Saturday evening, 12 September.

Investigators have identified similarities between the four deaths. The women were found partially naked, had visible bruising and were discovered in the same general area.



However, police have not confirmed that the cases are linked or that a serial killer is responsible.

SAPS has urged the public not to speculate while detectives investigate the circumstances surrounding each death.

SAPS steps up investigation

Acting National Commissioner Lieutenant General Puleng Dimpane ordered Gauteng police to establish a multidisciplinary task team to probe the deaths.



Specialist detectives from the Murder and Robbery Unit and Investigative Psychology Unit will form part of the investigation.

Gauteng Deputy Provincial Commissioner Major General Mbuso Khumalo will oversee the team.

Detectives will now examine the circumstances surrounding each death, including whether the same person or group could be responsible.



Warning issued to women

SAPS has urged women in and around Rhodesfield to take extra precautions, particularly when walking or exercising alone.

Police advised residents to avoid isolated areas and travel in groups where possible.

“The safety of women remains a priority for SAPS, and the police will not wait for further incidents before taking decisive action,” SAPS said.



Officers have also appealed to residents, motorists and private security personnel who may have witnessed suspicious activity in the area to come forward.

Anyone with information can contact Warrant Officer Elvis Manyike on 082 465 7249 or report it anonymously through the MySAPS App.

World.title: South Africa’s largest airline announces new regional route
World.content:
South Africans will have a new direct flight option to Zambia, with FlySafair launching a new regional route between Johannesburg and Lusaka.

The airline will operate flights between OR Tambo International Airport and Kenneth Kaunda International Airport five times a week, adding another connection between the two neighbouring countries.

Flights will operate on Mondays, Wednesdays, Thursdays, Fridays and Sundays.



Full Johannesburg–Lusaka, Zambia flight schedule

The new regional route will operate according to the following schedule:

Route Departure Arrival Days Johannesburg → Lusaka 07:50 from OR Tambo 09:50 in Lusaka Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Sunday Lusaka → Johannesburg 10:50 from Kenneth Kaunda 12:50 at OR Tambo Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Sunday

All times are local.

What flights will cost

Fares start at R2 800 for flights from Johannesburg to Lusaka and R3 000 for return flights, excluding surcharges.



Fares are subject to availability and may change.

FlySafair says the route was introduced in response to demand for travel between the two cities.

“Zambia has long been on our radar, and Lusaka is a route our customers have been asking about,” said Kirby Gordon, Chief Marketing Officer at FlySafair. 

“The Johannesburg–Lusaka corridor carries a significant mix of business and leisure travellers, as well as South Africans and Zambians travelling to see family and friends. We’re proud to bring our fares and our reliability to this route and to make the connection between our two countries more accessible than it has been.” Gordon added.

More options for Zambia travel

Lusaka is not only Zambia’s capital but also an important business and transport hub for the region.

The new route will give South African travellers direct access to the capital, while Lusaka also serves as a gateway to destinations including Livingstone and Victoria Falls, the Lower Zambezi and South Luangwa national parks.



The route could also appeal to business travellers, with Zambia and South Africa having significant commercial and investment ties.

The new route also comes with relatively straightforward entry requirements for South African travellers.

South African passport holders do not need a visa to enter Zambia for visits. South Africa is included on Zambia’s official list of nationalities exempt from visa requirements.



Zambia’s immigration authorities state that ordinary visitors and tourists can be granted up to 90 days within a 12-month period, although the actual period granted is determined on entry.

Travellers should still have a valid passport, with Zambia requiring at least six months’ validity from the date of entry and three blank pages.

World.title: Changed your surname? Here’s how to get a new Smart ID
World.content:
Got a new surname? Here's what you need to know about updating your official documents. Image: file / canva

Changed your surname after getting married, divorced or for another reason? There are two separate steps to getting a Smart ID with your new details.

First, your surname must be officially changed or recorded by Home Affairs. Only after that has been approved and updated on the National Population Register can you apply for a new Smart ID.

Step 1: Change or record your surname

The process depends on why your surname is changing.



If it is because of a marriage or civil union, you can generally record your chosen surname with Home Affairs when the marriage is registered or afterwards. You may take your spouse’s surname, retain your own or use a double-barrelled surname.

If you are reverting to a previous surname after divorce, you can request the change using your divorce decree.

For other surname changes, you will need to submit a formal application explaining the reason for the change and provide supporting documents.



Home Affairs then processes the application and, once approved, records the new surname on the National Population Register.

Step 2: Apply for your new Smart ID

This comes after the surname change has been processed.

Once your new surname appears on your Home Affairs record, you can apply for a replacement Smart ID reflecting the updated details.



For a marriage- or divorce-related change, take your current Smart ID and relevant marriage certificate or divorce decree when required.

For other surname changes, keep your Home Affairs approval documentation, as you may need it to support the replacement application.

The Smart ID is therefore not what changes your surname. Home Affairs first changes the official record; the new Smart ID then reflects that change.



Once you have your new Smart ID, there is still some admin to do.

You may need to update your passport, driver’s licence, SARS and eFiling profile, bank accounts, medical aid, employer records, insurance, vehicle registration and property or bond records.

Keeping the same surname across these records makes it easier for organisations to verify your identity.



Can you still apply for the new ID card at a bank branch?

Yes. Once your surname has been updated by Home Affairs, you can use a participating bank branch that offers Smart ID services, provided the branch accepts your type of application.

Home Affairs has expanded its Smart ID services through participating banks, making it possible for eligible applicants to complete the application and biometric process at certain branches rather than visiting a Home Affairs office.

However, bank services and the types of applications they handle can differ between branches, so it is worth checking that the specific branch offers Smart ID re-issues before going.



How long does it take?

The timeframe depends on the type of surname change and whether Home Affairs needs additional verification.

Some applications can take weeks or longer.

If you need a new passport for international travel, it is also important to allow enough time for the surname change and subsequent document updates.

World.title: Updated rankings after Springboks power past All Blacks
World.content:
The Springboks claimed a 43-28 victory over New Zealand to claim the inaugural Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry title in Baltimore, ultimately finishing as 3-1 victors after bouncing back following a humbling defeat in the opening encounter.

On Saturday, the Springboks scored six tries to four to claim a comfortable win in front of a USA rugby record crowd of more than 68,000 – the majority of whom appeared to be expatriate South Africans.

Besides seeing the Springboks add yet another piece of silverware to their trophy cabinet, the latest result also enabled Rassie Erasmus’ team to gain another 0.76 rankings points.



South Africa now have a buffer of 3.94 points over the All Blacks in the updated rankings.

Meanwhile, in a Pacific Nations Cup semi-final match between Japan and USA in Higashiosaka, Osaka, it was the hosts who claimed a comprehensive 63-14.

Rank Country Points 1 South Africa 95.09 2 New Zealand 91.15 3 Ireland 88.08 4 France 87.43 5 England 85.68 6 Scotland 84.78 7 Australia 83.55 8 Argentina 82.24 9 Fiji 78.00 10 Wales 76.38 11 Italy 76.30 12 Japan 76.09 13 Georgia 73.94 14 USA 69.49 15 Portugal 69.39 16 Chile 66.94 17 Spain 66.83 18 Uruguay 65.75 19 Tonga 65.14 20 Samoa 64.73

The win confirmed the world ranked number status of the back-to-back world champions, which Rassie Erasmus conceded was not always easy for others to accept.

“I know we sometimes annoy other people around the world for the way go about things, or the angle we take on issues, but we really care the most about South African people,” he said.

“We enjoy the other people around the world, and we understand their opinions and love the banter, but there’s only one reason for us as a team and for us as a country, it’s for South Africa.”

The match was in the balance until the final quarter and although the Springboks won three successive matches to claim the title, Erasmus said the margins between the teams were minimal.



“I wouldn’t say we were the better team. At 60 minutes the game was still in the balance. We appreciate that we won but the margin between us and New Zealand is very small.”

World.title: This prime Cape Town land is on sale for R200 000
World.content:
Finding a plot in Cape Town for R500 000, let alone R200 000, is rare.

Once in a blue moon, an unbelievable property becomes available.

This is one of those instances.



Yet, attached to the unbelievable price is a huge caveat.

R200 000 Land on Auction

Four plots have an opening bid of R200 000 and no reserve.

The plots will be auctioned on 17 September and range from 379 square metres to 415 square metres.

But there’s a catch: each plot has been affected by a landslide.

In some instances, the homes previously erected on these parcels will need to be demolished.

Buyers will need to prepare for building costs and the steep insurance increases associated with buying this kind of land.



The listings suggest the body corporate will cover the cost of reinforcing the barriers on the four sloped plots.

But will that be enough?

According to a study published on ScienceDirect, 22% of landslide areas will experience at least 3 such events in 30 years.

Buyers should prepare for that.

If another landslide occurs, the home a buyer builds could be difficult to sell.

Insurance may not pay out because of the history.

Homeowners could also struggle to benefit from an area’s favourable property trends. They will need to disclose the landslide to any potential buyers.

De Tijger Property

Yet these plots will still draw significant interest.

All are in an estate in De Tijger.

Other properties on elevated plots are listed for R5.25 million.

A home on the same street as the affected plots sold for R2.7 million in July.

Beyond the estate, the average sale price in the area is R3 million.

So, getting land for sale closer to R200 000 is rare.

However, buyers may spend more depending on the auction action.

Buying at Auction

A no-reserve auction is enticing, especially with a starting bid of R200 000.

However, the eventual sale price is subject to confirmation and additional fees.

If a buyer wins the auction, they’ll pay a 2.5% deposit and a 10% auctioneer’s fee immediately.

They must pay the balance when the property transfers into their name.

Anyone interested in participating has to pay a refundable R50 000 deposit.

First-time buyers and novice bargain-hunters may want to sit this one out.

World.title: Springboks player ratings: Arendse, Van den Berg shine in Baltimore
World.content:
The Springboks saved their best performance for last as they went on to claim Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series with a convincing 43-28 victory (halftime 17-14) in the fourth and deciding test at the M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore, USA, on Saturday.

South Africa dominated for much of the game and finally put daylight between themselves and a brave but ultimately outgunned All Blacks team with an emphatic 26-14 second half performance in front of a heavily green-tinged 68,173 crowd – a record for a rugby match in the USA.

Ultimately, the Springboks outscored the All Blacks in tries (six to four) for the first time in the series as several players delivered heroic performances across the field, with scrumhalf Morne van den Berg producing a man-of-the-match performance, which also included a conversion.



Damian de Allende, Malcolm Marx, Pieter-Steph du Toit, Kurt-Lee Arendse and Cameron Hanekom also crossed for tries while Codie Taylor, Will Jordan, Ethan Blackadder, and Beauden Barrett (in the final minute) scoring for New Zealand.

Key Springbok player ratings against the All Blacks

Morne van den Berg 9/10

Delivered a standout, man-of-the-match performance after receiving a deserved start at scrumhalf. Besides controlling the game’s tempo, he was outstanding on defence, scored a superb try and even stepped up to handle goal-kicking duties late in the game.

Kurt-Lee Arendse 8/10

Reliable as ever, Arendse wreaked havoc from the wing by repeatedly slicing through defensive gaps, posing a constant counter-attacking threat, and crossing the line for a stunning solo try.

Damian de Allende 8/10



Put in a tireless 80-minute shift in the midfield, bringing his trademark physicality in defence and as a ball carrier, while also scoring another well-finished try.

Jasper Wiese 8/10

Provided immense forward momentum with powerful, non-stop carries and dominant physical work in the loose. He has got better and better as the series has gone on, and like the Springboks, he left his best for last.

Malcolm Marx 8/10

Anchored the front row with signature physicality at the breakdown, setting up the foundation for the forward battle and crossing the line off a powerful rolling maul. He has reminded everyone of his enduring class this series, and there is no doubt Marx is the premier hooker in world rugby.

Scorers:

Springboks 43 (17) – Tries: Damian De Allende, Morne van den Berg, Malcolm Marx, Pieter-Steph du Toit, Kurt-Lee Arendse, Cameron Hanekom. Conversions: Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu (2), Morne van den Berg, Manie Libbok (2). Penalty goal: Feinberg-Mngomezulu.

New Zealand 28 (14) – Tries: Codie Taylor, Will Jordan, Ethan Blackadder, Beauden Barrett. Conversions: Damian McKenzie (4).

World.title: 8 times South Africans made us PROUD on the world stage
World.content:
Eight times South Africans conquered the world. Did we miss any out? Let us know in the comments below ... Image: AI generated, for illustrative purposes only

South Africans, we’re a different breed. Last night’s victory in rugby’s greatest rivalry got us thinking about all the times we’ve genuinely conquered the best in the world, on and off a sports pitch …

Firstly, did you know we have one of the highest percentages of Nobel Peace Prize winners per capita? The highest are the Swiss, interestingly. Or how we changed the course of medical history nearly 60 years ago? And we can count one of the most statistically decorated golfers ever as ours?

EIGHT TIMES SOUTH AFRICANS CONQUERED THE WORLD

South Africans from all walks of life, from Benoni to Zwide, have put us on a global map. Image: File

It’s kind of our thing, backs to the wall, punching above our weight against all sorts of adversity.



So, here are eight verified moments where South Africans really were undeniably the best in the world …

1. FOUR NOBEL PEACE PRIZE LAUREATES

Albert Luthuli in 1960, Desmond Tutu in 1984, then Nelson Mandela and FW de Klerk jointly in 1993. Four Nobel Peace Prize laureates from one country in just 33 years. All tied to the fight against the end of apartheid, this feat puts South Africa in genuinely rare company on the world stage.

2. SPRINGBOKS’ FOUR RUGBY WORLD CUPS

Count them: 1995, 2007, 2019 and 2023. Four titles make the Springboks the most successful team in Rugby World Cup history. The first men’s side to achieve that, edging past our great rivals, New Zealand with three. Genuinely, objectively, one of the best national teams to play any sport … ever.

3. CHARLIZE THERON’S OSCAR

Benoni-born Theron won the Academy Award for Best Actress in 2004’s Monster, the first and only Oscar for acting won by a South African to date. Of course, the film Tsotsi won Best Foreign Language Film in 2005. The award is technically presented to the submitting country rather than an individual. So, we’ll take that, too.

4. WORLD’S FIRST HEART TRANSPLANT

Dr. Barnard put South Africa and Groote Schuur Hospital on the global map back in 1967. Image: File

On 3 December 1967, Dr. Christiaan Barnard led a 30-person surgical team at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town to perform the world’s first human-to-human heart transplant. It reshaped modern medicine and made an unknown Cape Town surgeon and hospital household names overnight.

5. ELON MUSK, RICHEST PERSON ON EARTH

South Africans either love him or loathe him, but the world’s richest man has a birth certificate from Pretoria. Granted, Musk left South Africa at age 17 and has publicly denounced the country on numerous occasions, but he did become the world’s first trillionaire in June 2026. That’s some kind of drive and ambition for you …



6. GARY PLAYER’S NINE MAJORS

Nine major championships and a career Grand Slam completed at just age 29. Gary Player is one of only five golfers in history to pull that off, next to legends like Jack Nicklaus and Tiger Woods. Player was born in Johannesburg and is still one of the most statistically decorated to ever play the game.

7. THREE MISS UNIVERSE CROWNS

Margaret Gardiner in 1978, Demi-Leigh Nel-Peters in 2017 and Zozibini Tunzi in 2019. Three South Africans that conquered the best in the world. Three wins ties South Africa with Sweden and places us among the top eight in Miss Universe history.

8. WORLD’S LARGEST RADIO TELESCOPE

The South African component of the Square Kilometre Array in the Northern Cape. Image: File

Not an individual but a collective cross-border effort, the Karoo desert in the Northern Cape hosts the mid-frequency component of the Square Kilometre Array. Its precursor, MeerKAT, has been operational since 2018 and is already the most sensitive telescope array of its kind in the world.

But what do you think? Did we leave any out? Are there South Africans more deserving than those mentioned above? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: PREVIEW of October 2026 SASSA Children’s Grants
World.content:
Here's a preview of October 2026 SASSA Children’s Grants, with trouble looming on all sides. Image: AI generated, for illustrative purposes only

It’s not great news for October 2026 SASSA Children’s Grants being disbursed in three weeks’ time.

With the grant set aside for more than 13 million recipients with children, it is, in fact, the largest state-run social-protection programme. And that’s why it is coming under fire from likely and some unlikely sources …

OCTOBER 2026 SASSA CHILDREN’S GRANTS

Firstly, there’s the payment date set aside for October 2026 SASSA Children’s Grants: Tuesday, 6 October.



That’s a longer-than-usual gap since September’s disbursements, 32 days to be exact. Of course, calendars ebb and flow, but the average gap is 28 days. And Older Persons get their grants paid sooner.

However, the next issue is likely to leave beneficiaries in a real state.

While the decision to initiate October grant top-ups is still to be decided, we are highly certain that R580 Child Support will not increase.



The South African Social Security Agency has not done so for consecutive years, and is even less likely to do so this year …

LOWER THE NUMBER BENEFICIARIES BY 2028

According to The South African, the agency must lower the number of Child Support beneficiaries by 696 000 by 2028.

According to the National Treasury, which decides SASSA’s annual budget, it must lower the number of beneficiaries like so in the coming years:



This year (2026), 248 000 must be wiped off the books

must be wiped off the books In 2027, they want a further 232 000 gone

gone And in 2028, another 216 000 beneficiaries are scheduled to be removed

beneficiaries are scheduled to be removed Leaving a total of 696 000 recipients on the chopping block

That spells three kinds of bad news for October 2026 SASSA Children’s Grants.

HOW MUCH WILL OCTOBER 2026 SASSA CHILDREN’S GRANTS BE?

It is unlikely that SASSA Child Support will see any top-up increases this coming month. Image: File

As mentioned, at the time of publishing, the amounts for most October 2026 SASSA Children’s Grants themselves are unchanged:

Child Support pays R580 , up by R20 from R560 back in April 2026

, up by from R560 back in April 2026 Foster Child pays R1 290 , up by R40 from R1 250 back in April 2026

, up by from R1 250 back in April 2026 Care Dependency pays R2 400 up by R80 from R2 320 back in April 2026.

There have been scattered reports that SASSA Foster Care is scheduled for a R10 bump from R1 290 to R1 300. However, this is yet to be made official by the agency.



INCOME ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS FOR SASSA CHILDREN’S GRANTS

Likewise, applicants should always keep up to date with any revised income eligibility requirements.

Previously, a single caregiver on Child Support could earn R5 100 per month and still qualify. Now that limit has increased to R5 800.

And for married couples looking after a minor, the figure increases from R10 200 to R11 600 per month. This is good news for those earning extra on the side.



Tallied up annually, that equates to R69 600 (single person) and R139 200 (couple).

Note that there is no asset portion to the Child Support means test, like there is with SASSA Old-Age Grants.

Also, the agency now claims maximum wait times of just 90 minutes at SASSA offices. This is due to self-service kiosks with Wi-Fi where beneficiaries can complete eLife and biometric verification.



SAME-DAY SERVICE FOR OCTOBER 2026 CHILDREN’S GRANTS

SASSA Child Support is credited with largely eliminating malnutrition and stunting in early days of child development. Image: File

Better still, the agency says most October 2026 SASSA Children’s Grants can be approved on the same day. Previously, the waiting period used to be three months.

However, if you have all your documents in order on your first visit, you could walk away with an approved grant right there and then.

Here’s what you must remember to bring to your application appointment:



Valid identity documents (IDs) – preferably Smart ID cards – and birth certificates of you, your child and spouse (if married).

Proof of marital status (marriage, birth or death certificate of your spouse).

Proof of income (you and your spouse).

Certified three-month bank statement, not older than three months.

bank statement, not older than three months. Proof of address (a utility statement with your name on it that’s not more the three-months old).

World.title: Fourth Kempton Park victim found in sports gear
World.content:
KEMPTON PARK - Police are warning women in and around Kempton Park, particularly the Rhodesfield area, to exercise extreme caution following the discovery of the bodies of four women in the same area over a period of approximately two months.

Police are looking for multiple suspects following the harrowing discovery.

The fourth victim found was allegedly wearing sports gear.

Police spokesperson Brigadier Athlenda Mathe said preliminary information gathered by detectives indicates concerning similarities in the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

“The bodies of the women were found half naked and with visible bruising and the discovery sites are located within the same vicinity.

“While investigations are still underway and SAPS has not, at this stage, confirmed that the deaths are linked to a serial killer, the similarities are sufficiently concerning for the police to issue a public warning and intensify investigations,” Mathe said.

Acting National Police Commissioner, Lieutenant General Puleng Dimpane, has directed the Gauteng Provincial Commissioner to immediately establish a dedicated multidisciplinary task team to investigate these cases and determine whether there are links between the incidents.

“The task team will comprise detectives from specialised units, including the Murder and Robbery Unit and the Investigative Psychology Unit, as well as other relevant disciplines and resources required to urgently advance the investigation.

“SAPS is appealing to anyone who may have information that could assist the investigation, particularly residents, motorists, security personnel and members of the community who may have observed suspicious activity in the Rhodesfield and surrounding areas, to come forward,” Mathe added.

Members of the public with information can contact Warrant Officer Elvis Manyike on 082 465 7249 or provide information anonymously through the MySAPS APP.

World.title: Two minors among eight killed in Mpumalanga head-on collision
World.content:
ERMELO - Eight people were killed in a head-on collision on the N17 toll road between Ermelo and Davel, near the Ermelo Toll Plaza, on Sunday morning at around 1.30am.

The collision happened between a Toyota and a Volkswagen sedan.

The deceased include two minors and six adults. Seven of the victims were occupants in the VW sedan, while the eighth victim was the driver of the Toyota sedan, who was the sole occupant of the vehicle at the time of the crash. No further injuries were recorded.

Mpumalanga MEC for Community Safety, Security and Liaison, Jackie Macie, sent condolences to the bereaved families and urged motorists to exercise greater caution on the road.

"Motorists must obey the rules of the road and adjust their driving in line with prevailing weather and road conditions. Greater vigilance is a must, especially when visibility is affected," Macie stated.

The cause of the crash is not yet known.

“However reckless and negligent driving cannot be ruled out. An investigation has already commenced.”

World.title: Five arrested for the rape of an e-hailing driver
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Steenberg police in Cape Town have arrested five suspects for the kidnapping and rape of a 25-year-old e-hailing driver.

Police have alleged the victim was lured to meet a woman he had met through his e-hailing business, before being kidnapped and held for ransom.

His brother was contacted and told to pay R4000 for his release.

Police tracked the victim using his vehicle tracker and found him in Heathfield.

Two women, aged 23 and 34, and three men aged 16, 42 and 48 have been arrested.

They're expected to appear in the Wynberg Magistrate’s Court tomorrow.

World.title: ‘I wish SAFA was run professionally’ - Sandile Zungu
World.content:
MIDRAND - Amazulu Chairperson Sandile Zungu is calling for changes to the SAFA statutes to help the organisation run more efficiently.

Zungu lost the SAFA presidential race, receiving 82 votes to incumbent Danny Jordaan’s 157.

The AmaZulu Chairperson won't put himself through the same process again unless things are different.

"I wish SAFA was run professionally. I really wish it was run professionally, and there could be, you know, certainty that if you entered any race involving SAFA that you'll be assured of, you know, fair play because it would be a much easier decision.

“If I was to throw myself into a same environment with the same kind of rules, that is what is called classical stupidity.

You're doing the same thing and expecting different outcomes. I do hope that the, they call it the cadreship, that is given the task of leading SAFA in the next four years. Among their responsibilities would be to reform SAFA, its statutes, so that SAFA is well positioned to become a truly world-class organisation."

World.title: When science meets humanities
World.content:
PRETORIA - It was the perfect blend of the sciences and the humanities as hundreds of pupils gathered for this year's Roboticon.

The event is a competition where pupils display their tech savviness through robotics and coding.

This year’s theme explored how these skills can enhance and preserve Music, Art, and Cultural Heritage.

More than 450 school children and 160 teams gathered at Pretoria’s Heartfelt Arena for the occasion.

Live demos and games marked the day, aimed at inspiring young people to learn important digital skills in a changing world.

World.title: ‘I’m ready to serve you’ - EFF’s Dr Tlaleng Mofokeng tells Joburg
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - EFF Johannesburg mayoral candidate Dr Tlaleng Mofokeng said she is ready to serve.

She has asked for support from fellow party members to rebuild the city of gold.

Mofokeng was speaking at the party's manifesto rally.

“Here's what I'm asking from all of you Johannesburg fighters in the arena. Create Johannesburg with us, so we can focus on structural changes that are required for sustainable change.

“Create Johannesburg, create Jozi with us where it's a collective mandate is to continue to question every single thing we are inheriting in that council and to accept that nothing is just the way things are.

“In order to move fast to where we need to go in terms of our economy, social, health, development, peace and security, you need the EFF and me as your leader in the City of Johannesburg who is multifaceted and comes to this job inspired, energetic, agile, with a technical expertise and a world-renowned expertise.

“I'm ready to serve you and to be in partnership with various sectors and citizens.,” she said.

World.title: China, Russia, India seek economic cooperation at BRICS
World.content:
NEW DELHI - BRICS leaders including China, Russia and India entered a second day of talks in New Delhi on Sunday, discussing "inclusive global growth", after reaching rare agreement calling for calm in the Middle East.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for "cooperation" within the bloc, which he has said represents "50 percent of the world's population, 40 percent of global GDP and more than 25 percent of global trade".

"The power of BRICS lies in our diversity and cooperation," Modi told leaders, including Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, on the final day of talks.

BRICS was created in 2009 as a forum for major emerging economies seeking greater influence in institutions dominated by Western powers. The group is seeking to bolster its global influence and address conflict, trade turbulence and energy security.

"We have tried to push inclusive global growth," Modi said.

"We may be rooted in different realities, but together we rise through cooperation and blossom for humanity," he said.

- 'Maximum restraint' -

The first day of the summit on Saturday was dominated by the conflict in the Middle East.

BRICS foreign ministers had failed to agree on a joint statement in New Delhi in May, with Iran, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates divided over the war that began with US-Israeli strikes on February 28.

However, leaders -- who also included Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian -- issued a statement after intense diplomatic efforts by host India.

"We express deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in Middle East/West Asia," the joint statement said, adding that the BRICS countries "call for exercising maximum restraint".

Modi maintains cordial relations with both Iran and US ally Israel, but is also careful to strike a delicate balance in India's ties with Washington.

India has navigated the energy crisis caused by the US-Iran war in part by turning to Russia, despite Moscow's war in Ukraine and pressure from Washington and other Western capitals.

- 'Advancing together' -

Xi's participation in BRICS is also important because it is his first visit to neighbouring India since 2019, and the biggest step yet in a cautious thaw between the nuclear-armed rivals.

His visit comes six years after a deadly military clash along the disputed Tibetan border between China and India, with ties gradually improving through restored flights, visas and high-level contacts.

"Although our two countries are different in many respects, they are fully capable of complementing each other's strengths, supporting one another, achieving mutual success and advancing together," Xi said as he met Modi, according to a video released by New Delhi.

The underlying territorial dispute remains unresolved, and both sides retain heavy military deployments along their roughly 3,500-kilometre (2,175-mile) high-altitude border.

India's foreign ministry said in a statement after the meeting that "the two leaders expressed commitment to a fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary question".

Deep mistrust remains, with a widening trade deficit and strategic rivalry complicating ties.

"Both sides should... work hand-in-hand to promote high-quality major financial cooperation, advocate an equal and sustainable global order, and foster an economic globalisation that is open and inclusive," Xi said.

Xi's visit was the target of protests by dozens of Tibetans in New Delhi, exiles like their Buddhist leader, the Dalai Lama, who has lived in India since fleeing a Chinese crackdown in 1959.

World.title: 'Second life': Nepal tunnel survivor recalls ordeal
World.content:
NEPAL - For 10 days, Nepali hydropower worker Sanjay Sah survived in darkness inside a flooded tunnel, drinking muddy water and losing all sense of time as he desperately prayed for rescue.

When a disaster response team finally pulled him to safety on September 4, Sah's first question showed how deeply the ordeal had disoriented him.

"When I was rescued I first asked, how many days has it been?" Sah, 30, told AFP in an interview, while on his way back home in Saptari district Sunday.

"He said that it has been 10 days. I thought it had been just a few days."

Sah was among hundreds of workers at a series of hydropower projects hit by the catastrophic August 26 flood, triggered by a glacial mountain collapse on the China-Nepal border.

Sah's extraordinary survival was a rare ray of hope after a disaster that killed at least 1,429 people and left more than 5,640 missing, the majority in Nepal.

Struggling to hold back tears as friends and family welcomed him with garlands and a cake, Sah recalled how the disaster struck with stunning speed.

World.title: Why public anger against Ruto is boiling
World.content:
Three in four Kenyans believe the country is headed in the wrong direction, the highest level recorded in more than three years of tracking, according to a TIFA Research poll released this week.
