World.title: Police to restrict access to CBD during Linda Mwananchi Nairobi rally
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi officials during a rally. [Courtesy]

Organisers of the Linda Mwananchi rally and their supporters will not be allowed to access Nairobi’s Central Business District (CBD), Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud has warned.

According to Mohamud, police had received notification of the planned rally, which is scheduled to take place at Jacaranda Grounds on Sunday, through Embakasi East MP Babu Owino.

However, he warned that the CBD would remain off-limits, saying police would not allow Nairobi to become a battleground for political supremacy.

“The National Police Service respects the constitutional right of every Kenyan to assemble, demonstrate, express political views, and participate in public affairs, but that right must be exercised peacefully, lawfully, and with respect to the rights and safety of other Kenyans,” Mohamud stated.

According to Mohamud, they had received a tip that some individuals were planning to mobilise goons to disrupt the rally, prompting the directive to keep the CBD out of bounds.

“We have received some information, some credible information, that some individuals may seek to mobilise groups of unruly youths and goons to outnumber and intimidate and confront rival groups.”

“Therefore, I make a direct appeal to all political leaders, organisers or influencers to restrain their supporters and control their crowds. No political objective is worth the blood of a Kenyan,” he added.

Mohamud assured the organisers and those planning to attend the rally that police would provide security throughout the event and facilitate all lawful activities.

The Linda Mwananchi movement is set to hold its Nairobi rally on Sunday, September 13. The procession will start at All Saints Cathedral before proceeding to Jacaranda Grounds.

World.title: ODM vows not to interfere with Linda Mwananchi rally in Nairobi
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi leaders during a rally in Western Kenya. [Linda Mwananchi, X]

The Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) has said it will not disrupt the planned Linda Mwananchi rally scheduled for Sunday at Jacaranda Grounds.

In a statement on Friday, September 11, ODM Nairobi Chairman George Aladwa said the party had no business interfering with the rally, noting that Linda Mwananchi had a right to speak to Nairobi residents.

“I want to make it clear that nobody in ODM has any intention of disrupting or interfering with the Linda Mwananchi rally,” Aladwa stated.

He added: “We believe that political competition should be about ideas, policies and the ability to convince Kenyans, rather than confrontations between supporters of different political formations.”

Aladwa said ODM’s opponents had a right to tell Nairobi residents what they stood for and what they intended to offer Kenyans.

“The people are intelligent enough to listen to different political messages and make their own decisions,” Aladwa said.

At the same time, Aladwa said ODM was engaged in an extensive programme to market and strengthen the party across Nairobi as it prepared for activities to commemorate the anniversary of the death of its former party leader, the late Raila Amolo Odinga.

The chairman lauded Odinga for his contribution to Kenya’s democracy, the struggle for constitutional reforms and the political transformation of the country, saying his contribution could not be erased.

“His legacy remains an important part of ODM and Kenya’s political history. As we approach the 2027 General Election, our responsibility is to ensure that ODM remains strong, organised and firmly rooted across Nairobi,” the chairman stated.

“We will continue engaging residents in all constituencies and wards and explaining the party’s agenda to the people. I appeal to ODM supporters to remain calm and focused. Do not allow yourselves to be provoked into unnecessary political confrontations,” he added.

World.title: Ndindi Nyoro tells Ruto to keep off Tata Chemicals
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

PPK leader Ndindi Nyoro addresses a rally at Nambale market in Busia on August 30, 2026. [Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro has cautioned President William Ruto against meddling in the affairs of Tata Chemicals, Africa’s largest soda ash plant in Lake Magadi, Kajiado County.

Nyoro, who is the Peoples’ Party of Kenya leader, has accused President Ruto of an alleged plot to take control of Tata Chemicals through a shareholding scheme.

He said Ruto’s directive on Tata Chemicals closure raises concerns over the future of multinational firms and their operations in the country.

Speaking during a tour of Wote, Makueni County, on Thursday, Nyoro termed the Head of State’s move selfish, saying even if he had since softened his stance on the firm, it remains wanting for investors.

“His utterances were and remain wanting for external and internal investors. We don’t want investors to work in a bad political environment. Even if he seems to have made a U-turn on the matter, we are aware he has been pushing to be a shareholder in the company. We don’t want investors to be interfered with politically because we must create an environment where our people have access to job opportunities. It is almost reaching a catastrophic level in terms of lack of jobs for our people,” he said

The PPK leader warned that the country is in a bad economic state with a Sh13.5 trillion debt that is projected to grow further by next year.

“When Ruto exits next year the debt will be more than Sh15 trillion. The next president, who will be coming from the opposition, will have hard times in running this country. For every Sh100 that will be collected as tax from 2028, Sh91 will be used to repay government debts. We should not have time now to fight as opposition and also as Kenyans. We must hold hands and send the president back home because of his failures,” Nyoro said.

The MP urged opposition leaders to put aside their political differences and unite behind a single presidential candidate ahead of the 2027 General Election, saying that a united opposition would have a better chance of defeating President Ruto.

“If the opposition wants to defeat President Ruto, they must come together and present one presidential candidate. I am ready to talk to all the opposition principals,” Nyoro said.

Nyoro also outlined a raft of proposals he says could help revive Kenya’s economy and ease the financial burden on ordinary citizens.

Among his proposals is the use of the National Social Security Fund (NSSF) to strengthen the health sector. He argued that Kenyans should be able to access quality healthcare without being forced to bear the full cost of medical services.

Nyoro further proposed changes to the way education is financed, suggesting that bursaries currently administered through the National Government Constituencies Development Fund (NG-CDF) and county governments be channelled towards financing free primary and secondary education.

He said such an approach would create a more uniform education financing system and ensure that children from poor households are not disadvantaged because of their parents' inability to meet school-related expenses.

Nyoro's proposals come amid growing debate over the country's economic direction, the cost of living, access to healthcare and the financing of education.

World.title: Mama Tutam acquitted of Sh25m fraud, says Nigerian tycoon cost her marriage
World.content:
Nairobi Woman Representative aspirant Faith Mwikali Ndiwa, alias Faith Nguthu addresses journalists at the Milimani Law Courts in Nairobi on September 9, 2026. [David Gichuru, Standard]

A Nairobi Woman Representative aspirant has confessed the frustrations and embarrassment that befell her after befriending a wealthy Nigerian businessman who later accused her of defrauding him of Sh25 million.

Faith Mwikali Ndiwa, alias Faith Nguthu, popularly known as Mama Tutam, said she was kicked out of her marriage after the father of her three children discovered reports linking her to an alleged love affair with Nigerian investor Jude Olabayo Veracruz.

World.title: Sifuna hits back at Ruto over opposition agenda
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna promised to introduce austerity measures if the opposition takes power.

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna has hit back at President William Ruto after the Head of State accused the united opposition of lacking a clear policy agenda ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Speaking in the Senate, Sifuna, who has been fronted as a potential presidential candidate in the coming elections, said the opposition’s immediate plan was to restore meritocracy in government and remove Ruto from power.

Sifuna also questioned government spending, citing claims that Sh12 billion had been spent on hospitality at State House at a time when the country was facing financial constraints.

“We are being told that Sh12 billion was spent on hospitality at State House, in a country where we are told we have no cash for capitation. So those of you who ask us for a plan, ours is to send you home,” Sifuna said.

The senator further promised to introduce austerity measures if the opposition takes power, arguing that government spending could be streamlined to free up resources for essential services.

“I believe in the first 100 days after we kick this government out, we should be able to cut out the fat that is being utilised at State House so that we can pay our teachers and fund our hospitals,” he said.

Sifuna’s remarks came a day after Ruto accused opposition leaders of using ethnic profiling and intimidation to influence voters in areas perceived to be opposition strongholds.

Speaking in Ngong and Ongata Rongai in Kajiado County, Ruto defended the broad-based UDA-ODM political arrangement, saying the pact was aimed at promoting national unity and ensuring equitable distribution of national resources.

“They are intimidating people along ethnic lines, telling them they must vote a certain way. Do not allow yourselves to be divided through tribalism and hatred. Their agenda is to spread tribalism and hatred,” Ruto said.

The exchange comes as political parties and leaders intensify preparations for the 2027 General Election, with the opposition seeking to consolidate its support base while the Kenya Kwanza administration defends its record and broad-based political arrangement.

World.title: Centum taps insider as Mworia exits after nearly two decades
World.content:
Centum Investment Company PLC acting Group Chief Executive Thomas Omondi-Achola. [Courtesy]

Centum Investment Company PLC has appointed Thomas Omondi-Achola as acting group chief executive, tapping an internal candidate to succeed long-serving CEO James Mworia, who is leaving to head Kenya’s newly established National Infrastructure Fund (NIF).

The transition, effective immediately, marks the end of an 18-year tenure during which Mworia transformed Centum from a small investment firm into East Africa’s largest diversified investment platform, the company said in a statement.

World.title: Industry Minister stresses need to build Egyptian furniture identity
World.content:
Minister of Industry Khaled Hashem stressed that the furniture industry is one of Egypt’s longstanding industries, with a rich history and an internationally recognized reputation, supported by promising competitive advantages and capabilities that qualify it to achieve unprecedented growth rates.

He noted, however, that the sector has yet to reach its desired potential compared with the scale of its actual capabilities.

The minister underscored the need to build a distinctive identity for Egyptian furniture and strengthen links between designers and manufacturers, particularly as design represents significant added value in the furniture industry. He also stressed the importance of developing skilled artisans to ensure consistent quality and maintain the competitiveness of Egyptian products in both domestic and international markets.

The remarks came during an expanded meeting held by the Hashem on Saturday with a number of furniture manufacturers, designers and producers of production inputs. The meeting was attended by Assistant Minister for Industrial Policies Maha Saleh, Federation of Egyptian Industries Deputy Chairman Mahmoud Serag, and Federation of Egyptian Industries Executive Director Khaled Abdel Azim.

The meeting aimed to hear the views and requirements of industry stakeholders, identify challenges facing the sector, and discuss ways to develop the industry and enhance its competitiveness both domestically and internationally.

Hashem said the ministry has adopted a working approach based on direct partnership and field-level engagement with experts and stakeholders across various productive sectors, with the aim of identifying actual needs and real-world challenges based on practical experience and translating them into clearly defined, actionable plans.

He explained that the ministry’s current vision seeks to keep pace with advanced global developments and achieve qualitative leaps in the volume of Egyptian exports.

The minister pointed out that the ministry had recently intensified field visits to a large number of furniture factories and manufacturing centers to assess production performance and identify mechanisms capable of translating the sector’s competitive advantages into tangible positive returns reflected in increased production capacity and improved quality standards.

The meeting reviewed a number of key areas for developing the furniture industry, including deepening local manufacturing and replacing imports in major projects, as well as activating digital platforms for marketing and supporting access to foreign markets under an integrated strategy aimed at ensuring sustainable growth.

Participants also discussed ways to open new export markets for Egyptian furniture, particularly in African markets, Libya and Iraq, in addition to working to overcome customs and logistical obstacles facing exporters. Such measures would contribute to enhancing the competitiveness of Egyptian products and strengthening their access to foreign markets.

The meeting also addressed the possibility of developing a comprehensive program to support small and medium-sized workshops operating in the furniture sector by providing specialized training courses to raise the efficiency of technical workers, alongside establishing governance, oversight and quality-control mechanisms to ensure that these workshops comply with standards and specifications.

The participants also reviewed a study on the feasibility of establishing qualified, integrated industrial zones dedicated to furniture manufacturing, bringing together various production inputs and complementary industries in one location — from wood, foam, glass and metals to research and development centers and logistics services.

Such zones would help reduce logistical costs and facilitate manufacturing operations for investors and manufacturers.

The Industry Minister stressed that upgrading national products to compete on global markets is a key objective requiring concerted efforts by various state institutions in cooperation with private-sector implementation partners.

He underscored the importance of integrating all components of the industry, from design, manufacturing, skilled labor and production inputs to marketing and exports.

Furniture manufacturers and designers welcomed the government’s decision to form a committee for giving preference to local products, chaired by the Ministry of Industry, affirming that the move would have a direct and positive impact on supporting the growth of the national furniture industry and enhancing its competitiveness.

Participants also praised the Ministry of Industry’s approach of maintaining direct, field-level communication with manufacturers and its commitment to listening to the challenges facing the sector and working to translate them into serious and actionable mechanisms.

World.title: Transport Minister inspects railway maintenance workshops
World.content:
Transport Minister Kamel al-Wazir on Saturday, September 12, 2026, inspected a number of main railway maintenance workshops in al-Farz as part of a wider tour of Egyptian National Railways facilities, reviewing maintenance, overhaul and technical safety operations for rolling stock.

Wazir inspected locomotive workshops, which prepare 30 locomotives daily and around 250 monthly, as well as facilities servicing Talgo, VIP, Spanish and air-conditioned Russian trains, with about 720 trains handled each month.

He also reviewed workshops operated by Interplast for overhauling and maintaining power cars, which prepare 116 cars daily, along with Talgo maintenance facilities and an extension for a workshop dedicated to seven new sleeper trains contracted from Spanish manufacturer Talgo.

The minister also visited the Egyptian Company for Railway Maintenance and Services (ERMA), where he reviewed locomotive maintenance and rehabilitation projects, including 41 EMD locomotives that have been completed.

Work has also begun on upgrading 100 Henschel locomotives in cooperation with US-based PRL, with the first five already under development. Wazir inspected CNC boring equipment and locally manufactured spare parts.

The minister ordered that no train leave a workshop until its technical condition and operational readiness have been fully verified, stressing that strict maintenance standards are essential to safe and reliable rail services.

He said a comprehensive workshop modernization plan includes upgrading 33 existing facilities and building 11 new ones, eight of which have been completed, while work continues on the remaining three.

During a meeting with train drivers, Wazir stressed that skilled personnel are a cornerstone of railway development and called for continued training, qualification and strict compliance with operating and safety rules.

The transport minister also stressed the need for a reward-and-penalty system for drivers, noting that incentives for disciplined drivers have been doubled based on criteria including accident-free operations, keeping the ATC system active, passenger safety, adherence to schedules and locomotive cleanliness.

World.title: Egyptian ambassador to Ramallah presents credentials to Palestinian president
World.content:
Egypt’s Ambassador to Palestine Bassem Abdel Hady, head of the Egyptian mission in Ramallah, presented his credentials to Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday during an official ceremony.

Abdel Hady conveyed a message from President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi to Abbas, reaffirming Egypt’s commitment to continuing its support for the Palestinian people across various fields and standing by them in defending their legitimate rights.

The Egyptian ambassador stressed that Egypt would continue to support the Palestinian people’s legitimate rights, foremost among them the establishment of an independent state along the June 4, 1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

Expressing his pride in assuming his duties as Egypt’s ambassador to the State of Palestine, Abdel Hady stressed that Egypt would spare no effort in supporting the Palestinian people.

He also emphasized that the Palestinian issue remains at the heart of the conflict in the region, adding that achieving regional security and stability requires a just and comprehensive settlement based on the two-state solution, leading to the establishment of an independent, sovereign and viable Palestinian state.

World.title: Egypt’s youth handball team crowned African champions after defeating Tunisia
World.content:
Egyptian handball continued its dominance of the African continent as Egypt’s 2006-born youth team won the African Nations Handball Championship after defeating Tunisia 31-29 in the final, held in Côte d’Ivoire.

The victory saw the Pharaohs retain the title and reaffirm their status as Africa’s leading youth handball side.

The title came after a fiercely contested and highly challenging encounter, with the two teams trading control throughout the match.

With the win, the 2006-born generation retained its African title, reaffirming the continuity of Egypt’s dominance across the continent from one generation to the next and underscoring the Pharaohs’ strength across all age categories.

The youth team’s triumph adds another chapter to Egypt’s dominance of African handball, as the national teams across various age groups continue to maintain Egypt’s position at the top of the continent.

World.title: Rescuers searching for 140 people from Indonesia passenger ship, official says
World.content:
Jakarta, Indonesia Reuters — Indonesian rescuers were searching on Sunday for 140 people ​from a passenger ship that was earlier reported ⁠missing in the Java Sea after 103 others were evacuated, ​one of whom died, a search and rescue agency official said.

The ​Virgo Transport 8 ship set sail on Saturday from ​the East Java city of Surabaya to the South Kalimantan city of Banjarmasin ‌before ⁠losing contact, the agency said.

I Putu Sudayana, the head of the agency’s Banjarmasin office, said in a video statement that 103 people had been evacuated using different ships and some of them would be taken to an East Java port.

Relatives of affected passengers look on as a National Search and Rescue Agency (Basarnas) officer writes updates on a whiteboard amid ongoing rescue operations on the stricken Virgo Transport 8 ferry, at Trisakti Bandarmasih Port in Banjarmasin, South Kalimantan, on September 13, 2026. INFUZ/AFP/Getty Images

Rescuers launched a search, deploying a team, ships and a helicopter toward the passenger vessel’s last known position, he said, without stating what happened to the ship.

Indonesia, an archipelago of 17,000 islands, relies heavily on ferries as a key mode of transportation, with sea routes ⁠more ​affordable and readily available than air travel.

However, ​safety standards are not always rigorously enforced, resulting in a relatively high accident rate.

World.title: Trump administration offers rare muted response on new sanctions against Israel
World.content:
President Donald Trump and his top foreign policy aide, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, have not condemned the United Kingdom, France, Canada and others for their planned sanctions on settlements in the occupied West Bank – a notable development from the self-described “most pro-Israel” administration in history.

Their ultimate position on the new sanctions remains unclear, current and former US officials told CNN. Still, the lack of condemnation thus far is notable, particularly given the administration’s past policies towards Israel and the Palestinian territories – such as the removal of sanctions on violent West Bank settlers – and the warnings from the top US diplomat in Israel.

On Wednesday, asked about the sanctions, Trump took an uncharacteristically reserved tone, saying that he would be “speaking to Israel.”

“I understand exactly what’s going on, but I want to find out why all of a sudden does that happen?” he told reporters. The UK briefed the US, including in a call from Prime Minister Andy Burnham to Trump, ahead of the Tuesday announcement, sources said.

The sources suggested Trump and Rubio’s reaction may indicate discomfort with Israeli policies in the West Bank. Despite Trump saying that he would not allow Israel to annex the West Bank, Israel has only entrenched its control of the territory, expanding settlements and seizing territory.

Palestinians stand near a burning car reportedly set alight by Israeli settlers attempting to disrupt them harvesting olives near Turmos in the West Bank in October 2025. Hazem Bader/AFP via Getty Images

Though the Trump administration is highly unlikely to levy sanctions against Israel, the lack of condemnation from the top of the administration in the days since the sanctions were announced is piquing interest from US diplomats and US allies alike, said sources, who wonder if Trump may land in favor of taking some action. Even the smallest measures against settlements would mark a major rift between Israel and its key ally, the United States, as it faces growing isolation from the international community.

Backing the sanctions, or even a continued lack of condemnation, may signal Trump’s mounting frustration with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu who faces an election next month.

However, sources say a response ultimately boils down to how Trump wants to respond – and it may be strategic, as the administration navigates a continued backing of Israel externally with growing internal discontent about the situation in the West Bank.

Rubio, who also declined to comment or condemn the new sanctions, nodded to that frustration on Tuesday.

“We don’t want to see anything destabilizing going on right now in the West Bank with so much going on in the region. We think it has implications as well on our ability to make progress with regards to Gaza and the 20-point plan and Board of Peace that we’re very committed to,” he told reporters.

“Obviously, we’re not going to do what the UK did,” Rubio said, but added, “We were made aware that they were going to make this decision. We heard their arguments as to why.”

When asked for commment the White House referred CNN to Trump’s Wednesday comments.

Former US Ambassador to Israel Daniel Shapiro said the lack of initial condemnation “represents at least some degree of recognition on the part of the administration that the violence by Israeli extremists at the West Bank, and the statements and actions of the extremist ministers in the Israeli government are becoming problematic.”

Secretary of State Marco Rubio speaks to the press as he departs Tel Aviv, Israel, in September 2025. Nathan Howard/Pool/AFP via Getty Images

The brief comments from Trump and Rubio stand in contrast to those from Amb. Mike Huckabee, who accused the British government of “Jew hate” – despite the foreign secretary being Jewish – and warned ahead of the UK’s announcement that it could have a “huge impact on British businesses.”

Those remarks had not been coordinated with the White House or the State Department, a White House official said.

A former senior US official told CNN that Huckabee’s “reaction was consistent with his own views, as expressed for decades, about Israel and about settlements and about the West Bank.”

“It’s probably what he expected, because many people would have expected that that would have been the administration’s initial response, based on their history and the views they’ve previously expressed,” they noted.

In the early days of Trump’s second term, the administration lifted sanctions imposed under the Biden administration on violent Israeli settlers. The US, unlike international partners, has not publicly condemned Israel’s plans to advance the E1 settlement project, which effectively divides the West Bank into north and south, making a contiguous Palestinian state virtually impossible. E1 also splits East Jerusalem – the envisioned capital of a future Palestinian state – from the rest of the territory.

Israel’s far-right Finance Minister, Bezalel Smotrich, has explicitly championed the expansion of settlement as a way to “bury” the idea of a Palestinian state. “The Palestinian state is being erased from the table not with slogans but with actions,” Smotrich said when E1 received its final approval. Israel captured East Jerusalem and the West Bank in the 1967 war. Both are considered occupied territories under international law, and Israeli settlements there are widely regarded as illegal.

Shapiro, now a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council, said that when it comes to the violence in the West Bank, “that’s something that Trump has leverage to force Netanyahu’s hand with a fairly limited action because of the election.”

Netanyahu “badly wants Trump’s support, explicit if possible, implicit if not, and certainly doesn’t want him to make some expression that suggests Trump thinks things would be better with a different government,” he told CNN. “I think Trump’s got a lot of leverage, but I don’t think he’s really used it yet.”

Another former senior US official expressed doubt that Netanyahu would rein in the settlers in before the election.

This former official called the planned sanctions “a warning shot.” Another US official questioned whether they will be effective.

“These sanctions coming now are rallying people around Israel and somewhat around Netanyahu, giving credence to his argument that the world is against us now,” they said.

World.title: An ambassador in Ljubljana, but not in London: Israel’s foreign policy shifts away from longstanding allies
World.content:
Gideon Saar smiled as he cut the blue ribbon outside the newly inaugurated embassy of Nauru in Jerusalem. Israel’s foreign minister described the tiny Pacific island nation of some 12,000 people as “one of Israel’s greatest friends in the international community.”

Two days later, it was Slovenia’s turn, as Saar cut the ribbon on a new embassy in Ljubljana. He praised the new center-right government for standing by Israel in the European Union, especially after the country had previously been one of Israel’s harshest critics. A large business delegation was brought along to show appreciation.

There was no such celebration in London, where Israel faced one of its sharpest diplomatic rebukes in years: a coordinated move by the United Kingdom and 11 other countries to impose sanctions and trade restrictions on Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. Israel has had no ambassador in London for nearly a year. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s intended envoy, his chief of staff Tzachi Braverman, was barred from leaving Israel due to a criminal investigation, leaving the post vacant.

The split-screen moment reflects a broader pattern in Israel’s foreign relations: As traditional partners in Western Europe grow distant, losing patience with the settlement expansion and surging violence in the West Bank, the right-wing government is cultivating ties with smaller or what it sees as more ideologically aligned countries, redirecting its diplomatic energy to other arenas.

UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband tied the new measures, announced in parliament on Tuesday, directly to Israel’s decision to push ahead with the E1 settlement project, which critics say would cut the West Bank in two and close off the possibility of a contiguous future Palestinian state.

A photograph taken from the E1 corridor, an area in the occupied West Bank, shows vehicles driving along the highway near the Israeli settlement of Maale Adumim, on September 8, 2026. Ahmad Gharabli/AFP/Getty Images

But the move is part of a longer-term shift. In September 2025, Britain, Canada, France and more than a dozen other Western states recognized Palestinian statehood. And this June, the UK, Canada, France, Norway, Australia and New Zealand announced a wave of coordinated sanctions targeting individuals and networks accused of financing and enabling settler violence.

Some of the states announced additional punitive measures: France barred far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich from entering the country, Italy opened an investigation into National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir over the treatment of detained activists, including Italians, after Israel intercepted an aid flotilla on its way to Gaza. The Netherlands declared both Ben Gvir and Smotrich “persona non grata” and approved its own ban on imports of settlement goods.

Not every proposal has succeeded, and Israel has so far managed to stall broader actions from the EU. For years, Israel used Viktor Orban’s government in Hungary to block EU measures. Now, following a change in leadership in Budapest, Slovenia has effectively taken Hungary’s place as Israel’s representative in Brussels. A push by France and Sweden for an EU ban on settlement trade was stalled, as were efforts to expel Israel from the EU’s flagship Horizon research program.

Dr. Rémi Daniel, from Israel’s Institute for National Security Studies (INSS) says the one comfort for Israel is that Germany and Italy have so far stuck to statements rather than joining the sanctions. “They are the most important EU member states because they have the power to block plans at the European level,” he said.

But the trend was still concerning, he said, because looking at the balance of power within the EU, “the swinging center is going more against Israel.”

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar, right, inaugurates the new Nauru Embassy in Jerusalem on Monday. Shlomi Amsalem/GPO

Even as ties with some Western European allies fray, others are deepening their alliance with Israel through defense trade. Last month, Israel signed a $3.5 billion air-defense deal with Greece, one of the largest arm agreements in Israel’s history. And in early 2026, Israel Aerospace Industries signed a $3.1 billion deal with Germany to expand its supply of Arrow missile interceptor systems.

Israel’s response to the new sanctions – and its attitude towards one of its oldest allies in general – has been openly combative.

Saar swiftly announced he would close the British Consulate General in Jerusalem, end UK training for Palestinian Authority security forces, and ban entry to a dozen British officials and lawmakers. “The British move is morally distorted and constitutes a blatant interference in the affairs of a sovereign state and its electoral process,” Saar said Tuesday.

Netanyahu labeled the UK the “Islamic Republic of Britain” on a podcast last month and has accused French President Emanuel Macron of fueling antisemitism by recognizing a Palestinian state.

A view of the British Consulate in Jerusalem, a day after Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said he would close it in response to trade sanctions imposed by Britain. Ammar Awad/Reuters

While relations with some Western allies cool, and even the friendly Trump administration in the United States appears to be growingly frustrated with settler violence, Israel has been pouring energies into other regions and redrawing its map of relationships.

Declaring 2026 “The Year of South America,” Saar has toured Argentina, Ecuador, Paraguay and Colombia and restored relations with Bolivia, Chile and Honduras. He also opened a communication channel with Venezuela for the first time since 2009, sending rescue teams to assist with earthquake relief last month.

New Israeli embassies opened in Zambia, Estonia, Moldova, Fiji and Slovenia. And Israel became the first country in the world to recognize the self-declared Republic of Somaliland as an independent state. Somaliland then opened an embassy in Jerusalem, where fewer than 10 countries have embassies, including the US. Argentina, Colombia, Costa Rica and the Democratic Republic of Congo have declared their intent to join the list.

Daniel Shek, a former Israeli ambassador to France, argues that this pivot comes at a real cost and says the government is damaging relationships built over decades on shared interests in economy, science, culture, security.

“They are sacrificing the alliances with the most significant countries,” he said. “If Saar thinks the Paraguayan economy can replace France as a partner for export and import, good for him.”

The countries involved in the sanctions, he said, are not ideologically hostile to Israel, just its actions under Netanyahu, Ben Gvir and Smotrich. “France, Britain, Italy, the Netherlands, are friendly countries fed up with this Israeli government’s behavior.”

Shek notes that the sanctions target the settlements, and not Israel itself, and that their practical bite, for now, is limited. Still, he says, they should not be underestimated.

“Once sanctions have been imposed, it is significant,” he said. “There are things that have been opened and cannot be put back in the bottle.”

World.title: Trump says Irish unification would be ‘fantastic,’ wading into sensitive topic during weekend visit
World.content:
Dublin —

President Donald Trump said Saturday that Irish reunification “would be a fantastic thing” during a bilateral meeting with Ireland’s taoiseach, Micheál Martin, something he projected is “going to happen eventually.”

When a reporter asked his view on the topic, Trump at first acknowledged his comments could inflame a politically sensitive issue before voicing support.

“Well, I don’t want to cause any trouble,” Trump said Saturday. “But I will tell you, I’d love to see it unified.”

The reunification of Ireland has long been considered a contentious issue, dividing opinion among the unionists, typically from Protestant backgrounds, who would like Northern Ireland to remain part of the United Kingdom and nationalists, typically from Catholic backgrounds, who would like to see it reunited with the Republic of Ireland.

For nearly 30 years, Northern Ireland was plagued by significant sectarian violence and disorder, in a period known as the Troubles. Under the US-brokered 1998 “Good Friday” agreement, which largely ended the conflict, a majority of voters in border polls held both in the north and south would need to be in favor of reunification for this to take place. Wary of such sensitivities, US presidents have typically avoided explicitly commenting on the issue, even President Joe Biden, who frequently referenced his Irish heritage.

Trump’s comments were almost immediately met with pushback from the UK government and unionists. Downing Street pointed CNN to newly installed Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s comments in August when he downplayed the prospect of an imminent border poll in Northern Ireland. That is “off the table,” he said, later confirming he would “100%” follow the Good Friday Agreement.

Gavin Robinson, who leads the Democratic Unionist Party, said that Northern Ireland’s future “will be decided by the people of Northern Ireland, not by commentary in London, Dublin or Washington.”

However, Trump seemed confident the move would happen eventually and questioned how it could be a negative thing.

“It’s going to happen eventually. … I think it will happen now. You’ve got the right man over here to get it moving,” Trump said, pointing at Martin. “But yeah, I think it would be a fantastic thing. Now the UK will have something to say about obviously, but I think it would be a great thing.”

Trump touched down in Ireland on Saturday morning to hold talks with the country’s leaders before attending a tournament at one of his golf courses.

Trump’s son Donald Trump Jr. and his wife, Bettina, disembarked from the plane afterward and also greeted officials on the ground.

During the visit, President Trump heard an Irish band play the American national anthem, immediately followed by the Irish anthem, while Irish President Catherine Connolly stood by. Trump briefly answered a couple of questions after the courtesy call with Connolly, including one concerning traffic through the Bab al-Mandeb strait.

“Everything will work out just fine. It’s all going to work out fine,” Trump said.

This visit takes Trump out the US at a crucial time for him politically, just weeks before the midterms and as the Iran-backed Houthis’ rapid advance in Yemen threatens to open a second front in the war with Tehran.

US President Donald Trump is greeted by Irish President Catherine Connolly during an arrival ceremony at Áras an Uachtaráin. Charles McQuillan/Getty Images

During his time in Ireland, Trump will largely be shielded from the public and kept away from expected protests. Instead, he was ferried by motorcade straight to three official government residences in Phoenix Park, a huge urban park in central Dublin, which officials have closed since Friday night.

There, he held a bilateral meeting with the taoiseach and delivered remarks to business leaders at US Ambassador to Ireland Edward Walsh’s residence.

The president’s meetings with Irish political leaders will touch on bilateral economic cooperation, creating business opportunities for US industry, and discussing international issues of mutual interest, a White House official told CNN.

US President Donald Trump attends an arrival ceremony at Áras an Uachtaráin in Phoenix Park. Adrian Dennis/AFP/Getty Images

Protests of Trump’s visit

Trump’s visit presents a tricky balancing act for the Irish government. On the one hand, US companies, many of whom have their European headquarters in Ireland, are hugely important for the country’s economy. On the other, Trump remains unpopular with much of the Irish public.

Thousands of people joined an anti-Trump march through central Dublin on Saturday afternoon, several of them waving Palestinian flags.

“We don’t want him here,” Eudie Moriarty from County Clare told CNN. “We respect the president of America always. But not this president.”

Protests also took place in Doonbeg, the village in the west of Ireland where Trump’s golf course is located, and at Shannon Airport.

Anti-war activist groups have held demonstrations at the airport over the years protesting the US military’s use of the facility as a refueling stop for its troops, and then-President Ronald Reagan’s visit to Ireland in 1984 was also marked by protests.

Asked about the planned protests against his visit in Ireland, Trump said he was unaware of them.

“I didn’t know there was a protest,” Trump said. “It can’t be a very big one, because we’ve been all over Ireland today already,” though he had just landed in Dublin a couple of hours prior.

CNN photojournalist William Bonnett captured a small group of about 20 to 30 protesters in Doonbeg and Shannon on Saturday morning. One woman held a sign that read, “We do not like you here nor there. We do not like you ANYWHERE!”

After wrapping up his meetings in Dublin, Trump traveled west on Saturday to his Doonbeg course, where he attended the Irish Open tournament.

His son Eric Trump told Irish national broadcaster RTÉ that the golf course is the largest employer in the local area.

“Go down to Morrissey’s tavern in Doonbeg and hear from a real Irish person as to whether or not they like President Trump and the Trump family,” he said. “Go have them attest to what we’ve done for the country and what we’ve invested in the country and the love and respect that our family has always shown them.”

Connolly was among those who protested Trump’s visit in 2019 before she was elected to the ceremonial position of Ireland’s president in 2025. She was extremely critical of Trump during that campaign, describing him as “somebody who armed and funded genocide.” For his part, Trump referred to Connolly as a “he” in March when asked by an Irish reporter about her comments about “violations of international law” in the Middle East.

“Look, he’s lucky I exist, that’s all I can say,” Trump said. “If you’re gonna allow countries that are sick and demented — and they are demented — to have nuclear weapons, everybody in the whole world should be very thankful.”

If there was any tension between Connolly and Trump, he didn’t hint at it, calling her “terrific” during his remarks at the embassy later. In a statement released by her office, Connolly took a slightly more forceful course, saying she “conveyed the strong view of the Irish people that the normalization of war and genocide can never be accepted.”

While Trump said he hates “what’s happening with Europe” on immigration and trade, he gave effusive praise to the people of Ireland, one of two European Union countries where English is listed as one of the official languages, with somewhat of a backhanded compliment about their toughness.

“People love coming to Ireland. You know why? Because they love you. They love the people. There’s a friendliness. There’s, uh, there’s also a vicious and a toughness,” Trump said. “Let me tell you, you are some of the most vicious bastards I’ve ever (seen). But when you want to be nice, there’s nobody nicer.”

This story has been updated with additional developments.

CORRECTION: This story has been updated to reflect that English is the official language in two European Union countries. It was also updated with the correct 1998 signing date of the Good Friday Agreement.

World.title: Liberia: CBL, Commerce Ministry Push SMEs to Turn Market Opportunities into Growth as Liberia Expands Access to Finance
World.content:
Paynesville — Access to finance, business readiness and stronger partnerships between entrepreneurs and financial institutions dominated discussions on the second day of a national dialogue aimed at strengthening Liberia’s small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

Patience M. Jones, [email protected]

The dialogue brought together government officials, the Central Bank of Liberia (CBL), financial institutions, development partners and business owners to discuss practical ways of addressing one of the most persistent challenges facing Liberian entrepreneurs: access to affordable financing.

Atty. Andrew A. Tellewoyan, Officer-in-Charge of the Development Finance Section at the Central Bank of Liberia, provided participants with an overview of the Line of Credit (LOC) initiative, explaining how the financing mechanism is intended to support businesses, stimulate investment and create jobs.

According to Tellewoyan, the initiative is designed to expand sustainable access to finance, particularly for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), while encouraging long-term investment and private-sector growth.

He stressed that the financing is not free money but credit intended for viable businesses that meet established requirements.

“The objective is to improve investment, expand sustainable access to finance for businesses and facilitate trade,” Tellewoyan explained, emphasizing that access to capital must translate into economic growth and job creation.

Women-Owned Businesses Take Major Share

A major feature of the initiative is its focus on women-owned and women-managed businesses.

Tellewoyan said the programme seeks to ensure that at least 50 percent of supported businesses are owned or managed by women, as part of broader efforts to close existing gaps in access to economic opportunities.

He disclosed that women have already accounted for a significant share of beneficiaries under the programme.

Of the more than 350 MSMEs that had reportedly accessed financing under the initiative, approximately 64 percent were businesses owned or managed by women.

Tellewoyan said the result demonstrates progress toward expanding women’s participation in the country’s formal economy.

He noted that women play a critical role in supporting households and communities and stressed the importance of ensuring that they have greater access to financial opportunities.

CBL Launches Collateral Registry to Ease Credit Access

The CBL official also highlighted the recent introduction of a collateral registry system, which is expected to make it easier for businesses to obtain loans.

Previously, many entrepreneurs struggled to access credit because banks required high-value fixed assets as collateral.

Under the new system, businesses may be able to use certain movable assets, including vehicles and other eligible property, as collateral when seeking financing.

Tellewoyan said the initiative is intended to reduce barriers and expand access to credit for businesses that may not possess traditional forms of collateral.

“The goal is to create greater access to finance in the country,” he said.

The CBL, he explained, plays a regulatory and supervisory role in the implementation of the financing programme, ensuring that participating financial institutions comply with banking regulations and agreed financing requirements.

Call for Financing Beyond Monrovia

Tellewoyan also expressed concern over the concentration of financing beneficiaries in Montserrado County.

While businesses in several counties have accessed support, he said more needs to be done to ensure that entrepreneurs in rural communities, including farmers and small businesses, benefit from available financing opportunities.

He emphasized that the programme is open to businesses across Liberia and is not restricted to only the counties that have so far recorded loan disbursements.

“We want the money to go beyond Montserrado,” he stressed, noting that businesses in rural Liberia also need capital to expand their operations and create employment.

The CBL official said financing has supported businesses operating in several sectors, including agriculture, trade, education, real estate, services and hospitality.

Eligible businesses can access financing based on established criteria, their business capacity and the potential of their investment.

The maximum amount available to a single business, according to the presentation, can reach up to US$100,000, depending on the nature and capacity of the enterprise.

Interest rates, however, are determined based on factors including the level of risk associated with the business and the loan.

Commerce Ministry: Finance Must Follow Market Access

Delivering remarks on behalf of the Minister of Commerce and Industry, Deputy Minister for Administration Tarnue Jekeh said the dialogue was part of a broader effort to help Liberian SMEs gain access not only to financing but also to markets.

Jekeh recalled that discussions during the first day of the engagement focused on expanding market opportunities for SMEs, particularly their participation in public procurement processes.

He said access to markets and access to finance must work together if businesses are to grow.

“Once you have the market, the next thing is how do you finance your product?” he said.

According to him, providing businesses with funding without helping entrepreneurs understand how to manage and invest the resources could undermine sustainability.

“If you have the funding or grant and you don’t know what to do with it, it’s just a waste of time,” Jekeh warned.

The Deputy Minister said the government is prioritizing the development of agriculture and manufacturing as key sectors for strengthening Liberia’s economy.

He argued that expanding domestic production and exports could help address challenges relating to foreign exchange, trade and the country’s broader economic development.

“The government of Liberia recognizes that access to finance remains a major constraint to SME growth,” Jekeh said.

“For many businesses, limited capital restricts expansion, investment, innovation and job creation.”

He said the government’s financing interventions are intended not simply to make money available, but to help businesses improve productivity, respond to market demands and become more competitive.

SMEs Urged to Improve Their Readiness

Jekeh challenged entrepreneurs to strengthen their businesses by maintaining proper financial records, improving internal systems, developing clear business strategies and demonstrating responsible use of financing.

“Access to finance must be matched by readiness,” he said.

He encouraged business owners not to assume that financing opportunities are reserved for large enterprises but to seek information, ask questions and understand the requirements of participating financial institutions.

The Deputy Minister also called on banks and other financial institutions to clearly communicate their lending requirements and explore practical ways of expanding financing opportunities while maintaining sound lending practices.

Accelerate360 Identifies Finance as Major SME Challenge

Providing an overview of the second day of the dialogue, Prosper Doe Melomey, Chief of Party of Accelerate360 Liberia, said the programme is working to strengthen Liberia’s SME ecosystem, with a particular focus on improving the capacity and competitiveness of 165 SMEs.

The Accelerate360 SME Technical Assistance Programme was launched late last year and has since undertaken several interventions aimed at supporting entrepreneurs and institutions working within Liberia’s business environment.

Melomey said the programme recruited and trained business development specialists while also working with relevant government institutions to strengthen their capacity to support SMEs.

He disclosed that a national SME survey conducted under the programme received responses from approximately 1,500 SMEs across Liberia, representing roughly 100 businesses from each county.

The survey, he said, identified access to finance as one of the biggest challenges facing entrepreneurs.

According to Melomey, the findings are consistent with broader research indicating that a significant number of Liberian businesses consider access to finance a major obstacle to growth.

He said major barriers include high collateral requirements, interest rates, limited financial knowledge, weak financial infrastructure, lack of information and poor record-keeping.

“Poor record-keeping is another major gap in accessing finance,” he noted, stressing that many SMEs struggle to present reliable financial records when approaching banks and other lenders.

Melomey said the dialogue was designed to help entrepreneurs better understand available financing opportunities, including the Line of Credit programme, while creating direct engagement between SMEs and financial institutions.

He emphasized that financing programmes are not designed as handouts and that entrepreneurs must meet established requirements and demonstrate that their businesses are capable of using credit responsibly.

Building a Stronger SME Ecosystem

The second-day discussions underscored a growing consensus among government institutions and development partners that Liberia’s private sector cannot expand without addressing the persistent financing gap confronting small businesses.

For many entrepreneurs, access to capital remains the difference between remaining a small informal enterprise and expanding into a competitive business capable of employing more Liberians.

But officials stressed that money alone will not solve the problem.

They argued that sustainable SME growth will require a combination of market access, financing, improved financial literacy, stronger business management and closer relationships between lenders and entrepreneurs.

As Liberia seeks to strengthen its private sector and create more jobs, participants were encouraged to use the dialogue as an opportunity to ask questions, build relationships with financial institutions and prepare their businesses for future investment.

The message from the second day of the engagement was clear: Liberian SMEs need more than access to money they need the knowledge, systems and market opportunities to turn financing into sustainable growth, jobs and prosperity.

World.title: Former Maryland Quizzer Donates to Team, Pledges Help After Poor Living Conditions Exposed
World.content:
MONROVIA — A former Maryland County quizzer and coach, Freddie Goe, has donated US$35 to the county’s quizzing team following reports about the difficult conditions under which the players are staying during the ongoing National Quizzing Tournament.

By Peter P. Toe, Jr., [email protected]

Goe visited the team on Friday and also pledged to support their feeding and help improve their sleeping arrangements after reports that some players were sleeping on the bare floor due to limited mattresses.

The team is currently staying at a local school building in Day Break Mouth Open Community, where technical staff said the players have been facing challenges with accommodation, food and transportation.

The assistance from Goe follows earlier support from Maryland County Youth President Melvin Weah, who also provided assistance to the team.

The Maryland Students Union (MaSU) leadership also reported receiving US$10 and LRD$8,000 in support, including US$10 and LRD$7,000 from the Maryland Youth Association (MYA) and US$10 and LRD$1,000 from Marylanders based in Monrovia.

The MaSU leadership said the funds were being used to help cover transportation and feeding, while additional support is needed to secure suitable accommodation and provide some compensation for the players.

Speaking after the donation, Goe confirmed the support and appealed to other Marylanders to assist the team.

“As a former Quizzer and Quizzing Coach, I had to give back considering the challenges the team is faced with. We also seek the help of other meaningful Marylanders to contribute to the team for a success,” Goe said.»

Goe, a Senior Operations Engineer at the Liberia Electricity Corporation, previously quizzed for Central Site High School from 2013 to 2016 and later coached the school’s quizzing team from 2017 to 2022.

Meanwhile, Maryland has already recorded a win in the tournament, defeating Bong County 130–100, a 30-point margin. Team captain Leo Dickson was named Man of the Match after the victory.

Despite the win, members of the team continue to appeal for assistance with food, transportation and suitable accommodation as they prepare for their remaining matches.

World.title: Sleeping on the Bare Floor: Maryland Quizzing Team Battles Hardship for National Glory
World.content:
MONROVIA — Despite defeating Bong County 130 points to 100, a 30-point margin, in their first encounter at the ongoing National Quizzing Tournament, Maryland’s quizzing team is battling difficult living conditions, with some players sleeping on the bare floor due to a shortage of mattresses.

By Peter Poklo Toe-Jr

A photo shows members of the Maryland team sleeping on the floor, currently staying on a local school campus in Barnesville’s Day Break Mouth Open Community, where team officials say players are sleeping in open classrooms, highlighting the difficult conditions they are facing while representing the county in the national competition.

Despite the difficult conditions off the competition floor, Maryland delivered a strong performance against Bong County, securing a 130–100 victory.

Team Captain Leo Dickson was also named Man of the Match following Maryland’s victory.

In a video podcast Thursday after the game, Maryland Students Union (MaSU) President Eastman K. Toe appealed for urgent support for the team.

“It was on yesterday that we received the sum of L$8,000 plus US$10, which was L$7,000 from MYA President Melvin T. Weah and L$1,000 plus US$10 from Marylanders based in Monrovia,” Toe said.

He added: “Finance to cover transport and feedings. For the sake of security, we need unique accommodation and finance to help give little compensation to the players for encouragement.”

Toe said the team continues to face challenges with transportation, food and accommodation.

He said the team had planned to reach out to Maryland lawmakers for assistance but realized that many of the county’s lawmakers were not present in Monrovia.

Despite the challenges, Captain Leo Dickson said the players remain grateful for their achievement and determined to continue representing Maryland.

“We are grateful that we got this achievement. Through the challenges, we remained focused, and this is why we have come this far. But we deeply need our people to come through for us,” Dickson said.

The team’s Assistant Coach also acknowledged the difficulties facing the players but said their focus remains on succeeding for Maryland.

“We have been through the struggle. We have been through a lot of challenges since we arrived here. But we have Maryland as our focus to succeed,” the Assistant Coach said.

“But as players, this is not easy for us,” the Assistant coach added.

Technical staff member Samuel H. Griffiths Jr. said the team is particularly struggling with mobility and food.

Griffiths said the team’s sleeping arrangements are unsuitable because members are staying in open classrooms.

He said the team has largely survived on support from MaSU leadership and assistance from the Ministry of Youth Affairs, while contributions from other supporters have remained limited.

“The team need serious resources for mobility and food,” Griffiths said.

He added that the Maryland team is expected to be at the quizzing hall today to watch matches involving other counties.

Head Coach Edwin Lawal also appealed to Marylanders and other well-wishers to support the team as the competition continues.

“Your one cent means a lot for us. While encouraging our players, your support as a county is the most right now,” Lawal said.

Maryland is competing in Group C, alongside Grand Bassa, Bong and Nimba counties.

The team is now appealing to Maryland lawmakers, county authorities, businesses, Marylanders at home and abroad, and other well-wishers for assistance with food, transportation, suitable accommodation and financial support for the players as they continue their quest for national glory.

The team is led by MaSU president Eastman K. Toe, Head Coach Edwin Lawal, Captain Leo Dickson, amongst other.
