World.title: Swedes vote in election that could usher far right into government
World.content:
Swedes were voting in a closely fought election on Sunday (September 13, 2026) that will either bring a far-right party ​into government for the first time or shift the country back towards the liberalism it has long been ⁠known for.

Sweden's centre-left opposition holds a narrow lead over the ruling right-wing bloc ahead of the September 13 election for parliament, several opinion polls have shown this week.

But Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson, who has trailed in opinion polls throughout his four years in office, has been catching up in the ‌final weeks of campaigning, with rival Magdalena Andersson and her Social Democrats losing ground.

Mr. Kristersson has pledged to bring the far-right Sweden Democrats into government if his bloc wins.

"We can unify parties, voters and issues into joint ‌action. That's why we get things done," he told reporters this week.

Critics say his government's agenda is undermining civil liberties while ‌forcing ⁠immigrants to conform more closely to Swedish cultural norms or leave the country, urged on by both inducements and ⁠penalties.

"We've become a harder society, a quieter society, but also a poorer society as we've had growth far below our potential and where households see their pay checks buy less and less," Ms. Andersson told Reuters, adding that uniting people had made Sweden strong.

Supporters of the right-wing bloc say its policies have helped curb gang ​violence and cut immigration dramatically, and that a victory would ‌amount to a public endorsement of that approach and more in the same vein in the years ahead.

Electoral success for the Sweden Democrats is likely to be welcomed by Europe's rising far-right parties, boosted by a significant win in a German state election this month by the anti-immigrant Alternative for Germany.

Another Country

Polling stations in the EU member state of 10 million people, which ‌joined NATO after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, opened at 8 a.m. (0600 GMT) with exit polls due soon after ​they close at 1800 GMT and data giving an indication of the result at around 1900 GMT.

Voters in Rinkeby, an area designated by the police as extremely socially deprived, were worried things might get worse for ⁠them.

"They target Muslims; they single out Muslims and immigrants. But immigrants contribute to society," Kahin Ahmed, 57, a sociologist who came to Sweden from Somalia as a refugee told Reuters.

"A quarter of those working in healthcare are immigrants. If immigrants stayed home for a single day, ‌Sweden wouldn't function," he said.

Over the last four years, the ruling minority coalition — backed by the Sweden Democrats — has abolished permanent residency for refugees, tightened welfare rules and boosted expulsions of those without a right to stay.

Voting on Saturday (September 12) in Rinkeby in northern Stockholm, Sweden Democrat leader Jimmie Akesson said the suburb, home to one of the country's biggest Swedish-Somali populations, "doesn't look like Sweden".

The Sweden Democrats have pledged to ban both the niqab and the burqa if they get into government. Mr. Akesson told Reuters such dress "reflects values that I don't think belong in Sweden".

Building a government

The right has already agreed to form a four-party government led by Mr. Kristersson if they win, while Ms. Andersson's ‌path to power is more uncertain.

The election could ultimately be decided by whether the Liberals surpass the 4% threshold to win seats in parliament, bolstering a right ​wing that includes Moderates, Christian Democrats and, since being invited by Mr. Kristersson earlier this year, Sweden Democrats.

The Sweden Democrats have already spent four years propping up Mr. Kristersson's minority government in parliament, building credibility with the broader right-wing bloc.

Meanwhile, ⁠the rival blocs have converged on several voter priorities, including support for Ukraine, military rearmament and relief for households hit by the cost-of-living ⁠crisis.

While the opposition Social Democrats, Greens, Left Party and Centre Party broadly agree on the need for higher welfare and public spending, divisions persist on many issues, including immigration, where Ms. Andersson's party wants a more restrictive line than some of ‌its would-be partners.

They are also at odds over issues including a tax on billionaires and building new nuclear reactors, while the Centre refuses to support a government that includes the Left Party, increasing the challenge Ms. Andersson would face to form a ​cabinet.

World.title: Justice V. Kameswar Rao takes oath as Chief Justice of Patna High Court
World.content:
Justice V. Kameswar Rao was sworn in as the Chief Justice of the Patna High Court on Sunday (September 13, 2026) by Bihar Governor Syed Ata Hasnain.

The oath-taking ceremony at the Lok Bhavan was attended by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and other dignitaries.

Born on August 7, 1965, Justice Rao did his graduation with honours in Geography and LLB from Delhi University in 1987 and 1990, respectively. He was enrolled as an advocate in March 1991 with the Bar Council of Delhi and practised in the Supreme Court, Delhi High Court, and Central Administrative Tribunal's principal bench in New Delhi.

He was designated a senior advocate by the Delhi High Court in 2010. He was elevated as an additional judge on August 17, 2013 and became a permanent judge on March 18, 2015. He completed his law course from Delhi University.

In June 2024, Justice Rao was transferred to the Karnataka High Court, where he also served as its acting chief justice before his return to Delhi in July 2025.

World.title: House break-in attempt: Assam native held in Keralam’s Thrissur
World.content:
The Chavakkad police have arrested a 22-year-old man from Assam for allegedly breaking into a house near the Manathala Block Office at Chavakkad in Keralam’s Thrissur district and attempting to steal valuables.

The arrested is Radheshyam Garh, 22, a native of Naharkatia in Dibrugarh district, Assam.

The incident occurred September 11, when the doors at both the front and back of a house owned by the complainant’s father, located behind the Manathala Block Office, were found forcibly broken open.

The complainant and his friend entered the house to inspect the premises and found a man asleep in an upstairs bedroom. They immediately alerted the police, who reached the spot and took the man into custody.

During questioning, the police identified him as Garh. A subsequent inspection of the house and investigation revealed that he had allegedly entered the house, opened cupboards and other storage spaces, and scattered belongings in an attempt to steal valuables.

The complainant later came to the police station and identified the accused. As Garh does not understand Malayalam, the police arranged the assistance of an Assamese-speaking interpreter to ensure that he understood the nature of the alleged offence and the legal proceedings.

After completing the required legal formalities, the police formally arrested him at around 10.15 a.m. on September 12. A case has been registered against him at the Chavakkad police station. The accused was produced before the court and remanded in custody.

World.title: Kerala PSC faces legal dilemma over Crime Branch summons in Planning Board exam scam
World.content:
The Kerala Public Service Commission (PSC) is seeking legal advice on whether its chairperson and members should appear before the Crime Branch in connection with the alleged irregularities in a Kerala State Planning Board recruitment examination.

The issue is expected to come up for a crucial discussion at the PSC meeting on Monday (September 14, 2026), with the commission likely to take a final decision on whether its senior officials will report to the Crime Branch headquarters on Tuesday (September 15, 2026).

The Special Investigation Team (SIT) had issued notices requiring four PSC members to appear at the Crime Branch headquarters for questioning and recording of statements. The other members were expected to be summoned for questioning in subsequent phases.

At PSC headquarters

The PSC has taken the position that its members cannot appear as directed, citing the rules and protocol governing the constitutional body. Instead, the commission has indicated that its officials are prepared to cooperate fully if investigators come to the PSC headquarters to record their statements.

The Crime Branch, however, has reportedly rejected the approach, maintaining that appearance at the Crime Branch headquarters for questioning would not violate any special protocol or constitutional obligation applicable to the PSC members. The apparent disagreement has prompted the PSC to seek a formal legal opinion.

The legal advice, sought from its standing counsel and lawyers representing the commission before the Kerala High Court and the Kerala Administrative Tribunal, is expected to be considered at the PSC meeting on Monday, sources said.

At the same time, the investigators have indicated that the SIT could itself proceed to the PSC office if the PSC officials do not appear at the Crime Branch headquarters as directed.

World.title: Young elephant ‘Durga’ from Assam to reach Madurai Meenakshi temple; activists raise concerns over transfer
World.content:
A five-year-old elephant named ‘Durga’ from Assam is being brought to the Madurai Meenakshi Amman Temple in Tamil Nadu and is expected to reach the temple late on Sunday (September 13, 2026). The transfer, cleared by the Tamil Nadu Forest Department last week, comes amid recent proceedings before the Madras High Court over the movement of captive elephants to temples in the State.

Tamil Nadu Chief Wildlife Warden Rakesh Kumar Dogra said the ‘No Objection Certificate’ (NOC) for the transfer was issued last week. “Before the NOC, the District Captive Elephant Management Committee inspected the premises and checked the availability of facilities such as mud bath, water bath and walking space,” he said.

Chennai-based organisation Seva Trust had approached the High Court over the proposed donation of the five elephants from Assam to temples in Tamil Nadu. During those proceedings, the court was informed that the transfer to Meenakshi temple had received clearance, while the applications concerning the other four were pending. The court directed the State to take a decision on the pending applications within a week and posted the matter for September 16.

According to Mr. Dogra, applications for elephants proposed to be donated to four other temples and religious institutions are being processed. “Necessary inspections need to be done,” he said.

The five proposed destinations are Meenakshi Amman Temple, Madurai; Arunachaleswarar Temple, Tiruvannamalai; Kancheepuram Mutt; Vaitheeswaran Temple, Mayiladuthurai; and Ramanathaswamy Temple, Rameswaram.

In a separate case, the Madras High Court on September 2, set aside State-wide directions that sought to prevent temples from acquiring captive elephants. That judgment arose from the case of elephant ‘Lalitha’ and appeals filed by the Tiruchendur temple and the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department.

The Division Bench held that the Tamil Nadu Captive Elephants (Management and Maintenance) Rules, 2011 already provide for temples to receive donated elephants, subject to prior permission and safeguards. It set aside the wider directions affecting temples and privately held elephants, while retaining directions concerning Lalitha’s treatment, retirement and welfare.

Activists have raised concerns over the proposed transfer, particularly the need to transport five elephants nearly 3,000 km away and the speed with which the approvals have been granted. “A video of the elephant being sent to Madurai shows it in a forest area. If the elephant is owned by an individual who claims he is unable to care for it, why was it not at his premises?,” asked Arun Prasanna of People For Cattle in India (PFCI).

The elephants being transported are all young, ranging from five to 10 years old, raising further questions among activists about the circumstances of their transfer and the possibility of a commercial transaction. “If the individual cannot take care of these baby elephants, what happens to the mother? Taking care of an adult elephant is also significantly more difficult,” Mr. Prasanna said.

World.title: ‘80% Indians non-vegetarian, Indian non-vegetarian food is delicious’, says Rahul
World.content:
80% of Indians are non-vegetarian, and Indian non-vegetarian food is delicious, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said on Sunday (September 13, 2026), a day after an all-vegetarian spread was served at a BRICS Summit gala dinner.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosted the dinner for the leaders and delegates of the BRICS Summit at the Bharat Mandapam on Saturday (September 12, 2026).

In a post on social media platforms X, Facebook and Instagram, Mr. Gandhi wrote, "For the record: 80% of Indians are non-vegetarian. Indian non-vegetarian food is delicious. As are my sister's chole bhature." He also posted a picture of chole bhature on a dining table.

The remarks of the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha came a day after the gala dinner, which featured an elaborate all-vegetarian menu.

'Khandvi mille', a feuille steamed gram-flour roll, and 'khumb galouti', pan-grilled mushroom kebabs with mint pearls, were served as starters The main course offered 'paneer lababdar', 'gucchi marmik' — Himalayan morel mushrooms and tender asparagus — and 'carrot bean poriyal'.

For the record: 80% of Indians are non-vegetarian.



Indian non-vegetarian food is delicious. As are my sister's chole bhature. pic.twitter.com/8f6ziKjLan — Rahul Gandhi (@RahulGandhi) September 13, 2026

The other items on the menu included 'thakkali belle saaru' — light lentil broth, millet pulao, beetroot raita, and assorted Indian breads.

For the desserts, 'Old Delhi fruit cream with jalebi' and 'shahtoot phirni' wrapped up the menu for the VVIP guests.

The gala dinner was served to the accompaniment of a performance by an ensemble of over 100 artistes drawn largely from India, as well as other member countries of BRICS.

World.title: BRICS Summit 2026 LIVE updates: India focused on four pillars: resilience, innovation, cooperation, sustainability, says PM Modi
World.content:
As rising geopolitical tensions adversely impact ordinary people globally, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Sunday (September 13, 2026) that BRICS must rise through cooperation and inclusive growth to meet these challenges and blossom for the sake of humanity.

Interview | The Security Council is paralysed, but the UN is not broken, says UNSG Guterres

In an address at the concluding session of the two-day, India-hosted BRICS summit, the prime minister also flagged serious concerns over the “weaponisation of technology and critical minerals”, warning that it could hinder shared progress and prosperity.

Chinese President ‌Xi Jinping unveiled on Sunday initiatives in areas ranging from AI to trade to deepen cooperation among the “Greater BRICS” emerging economies, as Beijing seeks to weld ⁠the grouping into a practical platform for Global South development.

Also read | ‘From rule-takers to rule-shapers’: PM Modi’s big pitch to BRICS leaders in welcome address

The summit, attended by a galaxy of world leaders including Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, assumed greater significance as it unfolded against a backdrop of escalating geopolitical headwinds driven by the Russia-Ukraine war, West Asia instability and new U.S. tariff policies.
